title.zh: 卷76 列傳第41 文學
title.raw: 卷76 列傳第41 文學 Volume 76 Biographies 41: Men of Letters

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 文學《易》曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變，觀乎人文，以化成天下。」

translations.literal: Men of Letters — The Changes says: 'Looking at patterns in the heavens, one observes the seasons' changes; looking at patterns in human culture, one transforms and completes the world.
translations.idiomatic: On Men of Letters — The Book of Changes says: 'Observe the patterns of heaven to discern the changing seasons; observe the patterns of human culture to transform and perfect the world.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「言，身之文也，言而不文，行之不遠。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'Speech is the ornament of the person; speech without refinement does not reach far in practice.'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: 'Words are the adornment of the self; words without elegance will not carry one far.'

sentences.zh: 故堯曰則天，表文明之稱，周雲盛德，著煥乎之美。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao was called 'He who took Heaven as his model,' manifesting the title of civil refinement; the Zhou spoke of abundant virtue, displaying the beauty of radiant splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yao was styled the one who took Heaven as his model — a name that proclaimed civil refinement; the Zhou praised abundant virtue and celebrated its dazzling brilliance.

sentences.zh: 然則文之為用，其大矣哉！

translations.literal: Thus then the use of letters — how great it is!
translations.idiomatic: Such is the scope of literary culture — how vast it is!

sentences.zh: 上所以敷德教於下，下所以達情志於上，大則經緯天地，作訓垂範，次則風謠歌頌，匡主和民。

translations.literal: Above, it spreads virtue and instruction to those below; below, it conveys feelings and intentions to those above. At its greatest it orders heaven and earth, creates precepts and leaves models; next come folk songs and hymns of praise, to right the ruler and harmonize the people.
translations.idiomatic: From above it spreads moral teaching to the people; from below it carries sentiment and intent to the throne. At its highest it weaves order through heaven and earth, crafting precepts and leaving enduring examples; at a lesser level it takes form in ballads and hymns that guide the ruler and harmonize the folk.

sentences.zh: 或離讒放逐之臣，途窮後門之士，道轗軻而未遇，志鬱抑而不申，憤激委約之中，飛文魏闕之下，奮迅泥滓，自致青雲，振沈溺於一朝，流風聲於千載，往往而有。

translations.literal: Sometimes ministers slandered and exiled, gentlemen at dead-end back alleys, whose paths are rough and unmet, whose wills are depressed and unexpressed — from amid indignant constraint they send writings beneath the palace gates of Wei, springing up from mud and sludge to reach the blue clouds themselves, reviving the drowned in a single morning, flowing their fame for a thousand years — such cases often occur.
translations.idiomatic: At times it is the slandered minister in exile, the scholar trapped at poverty's gate — his road rugged and his talent unmet, his will stifled and his purpose unreleased — who, burning with indignation in the depths of obscurity, sends his writings up to the imperial gate; who bursts from the mire to the heights of heaven, lifts the drowning in a single day, and passes his name down through a thousand years. Such cases are not rare.

sentences.zh: 是以凡百君子，莫不用心焉。

translations.literal: Therefore all gentlemen without exception apply their minds to it.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, every scholar of worth devotes himself to it.

sentences.zh: 自漢、魏以來，迄乎晉、宋，其體屢變，前哲論之詳矣。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei down to Jin and Song, its form changed repeatedly; earlier sages have discussed this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From the Han and Wei through the Jin and Song, literary forms shifted again and again — a process that earlier critics have already treated at length.

sentences.zh: 暨永明、天監之際，太和、天保之間，洛陽、江左，文雅尤盛。

translations.literal: Reaching the eras of Yongming and Tianjian, between Taihe and Tianbao, Luoyang and the Left Bank of the Yangtze — literary elegance was especially flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yongming and Tianjian reigns in the south and the Taihe and Tianbao periods in the north, literary culture flourished especially in Luoyang and the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 于時作者，濟陽江淹、吳郡沈約、樂安任昉、濟陰溫子升、河間邢子才、巨鹿魏伯起等，並學窮書圃，思極人文，縟彩郁于雲霞，逸響振于金石。

translations.literal: Authors of that time — Jiang Yan of Jiyang, Shen Yue of Wu commandery, Ren Fang of Le'an, Wen Zisheng of Jiyin, Xing Zicai of Hejian, Wei Boqi of Julu, and others — all exhausted learning in the garden of books, thought reaching the utmost of human culture; brocaded colors dense as clouds and rosy mist, soaring resonance vibrating metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Writers of that era — Jiang Yan of Jiyang, Shen Yue of Wu, Ren Fang of Le'an, Wen Zisheng of Jiyin, Xing Zicai of Hejian, Wei Boqi of Julu, and others — had mastered the full range of learning and plumbed the depths of humane letters; their woven colors piled like clouds at dawn, their soaring music rang clear as bronze and bell.

sentences.zh: 英華秀髮，波瀾浩蕩，筆有餘力，詞無竭源。

translations.literal: Flowering brilliance splendidly issued, billows vast and surging; the brush had surplus strength, words had no exhausted source.
translations.idiomatic: Their brilliance bloomed in profusion, their style rolled like great waves; their pens never flagged, their words never ran dry.

sentences.zh: 方諸張、蔡、曹、王，亦各一時之選也。

translations.literal: Compared with Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang, each was likewise a choice selection of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the greats Zhang, Cai, Cao, and Wang, each stood among the finest writers of his generation.

sentences.zh: 聞其風者，聲馳景慕，然彼此好尚，互有異同。

translations.literal: Those who heard their wind — voice racing, shadow admiring; yet each other's preferences had mutual differences and samenesses.
translations.idiomatic: Those who encountered their influence were drawn to follow them, yet regional tastes differed, with points of agreement and divergence.

sentences.zh: 江左宮商發越，貴於清綺，河朔詞義貞剛，重乎氣質。

translations.literal: On the Left Bank of the Yangtze, palace tones soared and overflowed, esteeming clarity and refinement; north of the Yellow River, diction and meaning were upright and firm, valuing vital character.
translations.idiomatic: In the south, where tonal patterns rose with exquisite grace, elegance prized clarity and delicacy; in the north, where diction and thought stood firm and solid, weight was given to force of character.

sentences.zh: 氣質則理勝其詞，清綺則文過其意，理深者便於時用，文華者宜於詠歌，此其南北詞人得失之大較也。

translations.literal: Where vital character prevails, principle surpasses words; where clarity and refinement prevail, letters surpass meaning. Those deep in principle are convenient for timely use; those florid in letters are suitable for song and ode — this is the great comparison of the gains and losses of southern and northern poets.
translations.idiomatic: Northern strength let reason outweigh ornament; southern elegance let style outshine substance. Depth of thought served practical ends; literary brilliance suited poetry and song — such were the chief strengths and weaknesses that divided poets north and south.

sentences.zh: 若能掇彼清音，簡茲累句，各去所短，合其兩長，則文質斌斌，盡善盡美矣。

translations.literal: If one could gather those clear tones, select out these encumbered lines, each remove what is short, combine their two strengths, then letter and substance would be balanced and patterned, wholly good and wholly beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Had one been able to draw on the clear music of the south, pare away the heavy phrasing of the north, discard each side's flaws and join their virtues, letter and substance would have been perfectly balanced — truly complete in form and beauty.

sentences.zh: 梁自大同之後，雅道淪缺，漸乖典則，爭馳新巧。

translations.literal: Liang from after Datong — the refined way sank into deficiency, gradually deviating from classical norms, competing to gallop toward new cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Datong era of Liang, the classical tradition collapsed; writers drifted from canonical standards and raced one another toward novelty and cleverness.

sentences.zh: 簡文、湘東，啟其淫放，徐陵、庾信，分路揚鑣。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen and Prince Xiangdong opened the way to libertine excess; Xu Ling and Yu Xin parted ways and drove separate whip traces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen and Prince Xiangdong gave free rein to sensual excess; Xu Ling and Yu Xin then struck out on divergent paths.

sentences.zh: 其意淺而繁，其文匿而彩，詞尚輕險，情多哀思。

translations.literal: Their meaning shallow yet elaborate, their writing hidden yet colorful; words esteeming lightness and peril, sentiment mostly mournful thought.
translations.idiomatic: Their ideas grew shallow yet overwrought, their prose ornate yet hollow; they favored precarious lightness in diction and melancholy in feeling.

sentences.zh: 格以延陵之聽，蓋亦亡國之音乎！

translations.literal: Measured by the ear of Yanling — perhaps these are also the sounds of a perishing state!
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the standards of Yanling — were these not indeed the music of a doomed realm!

sentences.zh: 周氏吞併梁、荊，此風扇于關右，狂簡斐然成俗，流宕忘反，無所取裁。

translations.literal: The Zhou house swallowed Liang and Jing; this wind fanned out in Guanxi; wild simplicity flourished brightly into custom, drifting and forgetting to return, with nothing to take and cut.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Zhou absorbed Liang and the Jing region, this fashion spread through the west; unrestrained eccentricity became the norm, style grew ever more florid with no restraint in sight.

sentences.zh: 高祖初統萬機，每念鵶雕為樸，發號施令，鹹去浮華。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor at first unified the myriad threads of state; constantly thinking of carving crows into plainness; issuing orders and commands — all removed floating elegance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first assumed power, he resolved to restore plain simplicity — in every decree and command he stripped away ornament and show.

sentences.zh: 然時俗詞藻，猶多淫麗，故憲台執法，屢飛霜簡。

translations.literal: Yet the customs of the time in diction and color still had much lascivious beauty; therefore the law platform enforced the law, repeatedly flying frost memoranda.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fashionable writing remained excessively ornate, so the censorate repeatedly issued stern indictments.

sentences.zh: 煬帝初習藝文，有非輕側之論，暨乎即位，一變其風。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang at first practiced the arts of letters; there were essays rejecting light frivolity; upon reaching the throne, he transformed the wind entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Emperor Yang studied letters and even wrote against frivolous style; yet once enthroned, he changed the literary climate entirely.

sentences.zh: 其《與越公書》、《建東都詔》、《冬至受朝詩》及《擬飲馬長城窟》，並存雅體，歸於典制。

translations.literal: His 'Letter to the Duke of Yue,' 'Edict on Building the Eastern Capital,' 'Poem on Receiving Court at the Winter Solstice,' and 'After Drinking-Horse at the Long Wall Cavern' — all preserved refined form, returning to classical regulations.
translations.idiomatic: His Letter to the Duke of Yue, Edict on Building the Eastern Capital, poem for the winter-solstice court audience, and imitation of Drinking-Horse at the Long Wall Cavern all maintained an elegant style grounded in classical norms.

sentences.zh: 雖意在驕淫，而詞無浮蕩，故當時綴文之士，遂得依而取正焉。

translations.literal: Although the intent was proud and lascivious, the words had no floating turbulence; therefore the letter-composers of the time were able to rely on them and take them as correct.
translations.idiomatic: Though his purposes were proud and indulgent, his language never became florid or unmoored — so contemporaries could still look to his writing as a standard.

sentences.zh: 所謂能言者未必能行，蓋亦君子不以人廢言也。

translations.literal: What is called 'able to speak' is not necessarily 'able to act' — it is also that the gentleman does not reject words because of the person.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, those who speak well do not always act well — yet a gentleman does not dismiss sound words because he dislikes the speaker.

sentences.zh: 爰自東帝歸秦，逮乎青蓋入洛，四庾鹹暨，九州攸同，江漢英靈，燕趙奇俊，並該天網之中，俱為大國之寶。

translations.literal: From when the Eastern Emperor returned to Qin, reaching the time the blue canopy entered Luoyang — the four Yu families all arrived, the nine regions were uniformly one; spirits of excellence from the Jiang and Han, extraordinary talents of Yan and Zhao — all were covered within the heaven's net, together becoming treasures of the great state.
translations.idiomatic: From the fall of the southern dynasties to reunification under Sui, when all regions were united — the finest minds of the Yangtze and Han, the brightest talents of Yan and Zhao — all came within the empire's fold and became jewels of the new state.

sentences.zh: 言刈其楚，片善無遺，潤木圓流，不能十數，才之難也，不其然乎！

translations.literal: Speaking of harvesting its Chu — not a single good fragment was left behind; moistening wood and rounding streams — not even ten or so; talent is difficult — is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: One might harvest every fine fragment the Chu region had to offer, yet when it came to nurturing talent and letting it flow freely, scarcely a dozen could be found — such is the scarcity of genius, is it not?

sentences.zh: 時之文人，見稱當世，則范陽盧思道、安平李德林、河東薛道衡、趙郡李元操、巨鹿魏澹、會稽虞世基、河東柳抃、高陽許善心等，或鷹揚河朔，或獨步漢南，俱騁龍光，並驅雲路，各有本傳，論而敘之。

translations.literal: Literary men of the time praised by the present age — then Lu Sixian of Fanyang, Li Delin of Anping, Xue Daohéng of Hedong, Li Yuancao of Zhao commandery, Wei Dan of Julu, Yu Shiji of Kuaiji, Liu Bian of Hedong, Xu Shanxin of Gaoyang, and others — some soaring over Hebei, some walking alone south of the Han; all unleashing dragon brilliance, together driving the cloud road; each has his own biography, discussed and narrated.
translations.idiomatic: Writers of the day who won contemporary renown included Lu Sixian of Fanyang, Li Delin of Anping, Xue Daohéng of Hedong, Li Yuancao of Zhao, Wei Dan of Julu, Yu Shiji of Kuaiji, Liu Bian of Hedong, Xu Shanxin of Gaoyang, and others — some dominant in the north, some unmatched in the south; all burning with extraordinary talent on the same lofty road. Each has a separate biography and will be treated there.

sentences.zh: 其潘徽、萬壽之徒，或學優而不切，或才高而無貴仕，其位可得而卑，其名不可堙沒，今總之於此，為《文學傳》雲。

translations.literal: Among them Pan Hui, Wan Shou, and their sort — some learned excellently yet not practically, some talented highly yet without honored office; their positions could be obtained yet were low, their names cannot be buried and extinguished; now summing them here, thus is the 'Biographies of Men of Letters.'
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hui, Wan Shou, and others like them — some scholars of wide learning but little practical relevance, some men of great talent who never found high office — were humble in rank but not to be forgotten. They are gathered here in this 'Biographies of Men of Letters.'

sentences.zh: 劉臻，字宣摯，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Xuanzhi, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Xuanzhi, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父顯，梁尋陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Xian was Administrator of Xunyang under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian served as Administrator of Xunyang under the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臻年十八，舉秀才，為邵陵王東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At eighteen Zhen was recommended as a xiucai and became Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion for Prince Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was recommended as a xiucai and appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion to Prince Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan he was promoted to Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yuan of Liang, he was transferred to the post of Palace Attendant of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江陵陷沒，複歸蕭詧，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, he returned again to Xiao Cha and was made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell, he returned to Xiao Cha and was appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周塚宰宇文護辟為中外府記室，軍書羽檄，多成其手。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou Regent Yuwen Hu recruited him as Recorder of the Combined Inner and Outer Offices; military documents and urgent dispatches were mostly written by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou regent Yuwen Hu recruited him as recorder of the combined inner and outer offices; most military documents and urgent dispatches were drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 後為露門學士，授大都督，封饒陽縣子，曆藍田令、畿伯下大夫。

translations.literal: Later he became a Lumen Scholar, was granted the rank of Grand Commandant, enfeoffed as Viscount of Raoyang, and served successively as Magistrate of Lantian and Junior Grand Master of Jibo.
translations.idiomatic: He later became a Lumen Scholar, was granted the rank of Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Raoyang, and served successively as Magistrate of Lantian and Junior Grand Master of Jibo.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，進位儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted to Third Rank Commissioner with Equal Status.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Zhen was promoted to Third Rank Commissioner with Equal Status.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲之伐陳也，以臻隨軍，典文翰，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Director Gao Jiong campaigned against Chen, Zhen accompanied the army and managed official documents, and was advanced in rank to Count.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Vice Director Gao Jiong campaigned against Chen, Zhen accompanied the army as chief of documents and was raised in rank to Count.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇引為學士，甚褻狎之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong brought him in as a scholar and treated him with great familiarity and disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong brought him in as a scholar and treated him with unseemly familiarity.

sentences.zh: 臻無吏幹，又性恍惚，耽悅經史，終日覃思，至於世事，多所遺忘。

translations.literal: Zhen had no talent for administration, and his nature was absent-minded; devoted to the classics and histories, he pondered deeply all day long, and as for worldly affairs he forgot much.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had no gift for administration and was absent-minded by nature; absorbed in the classics and histories, he pondered all day long and forgot most worldly matters.

sentences.zh: 有劉訥者亦任儀同，俱為太子學士，情好甚密。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Ne who also held the rank of Commissioner with Equal Status; both were scholars to the Crown Prince and were very close in affection.
translations.idiomatic: One Liu Ne, who also held the rank of Commissioner with Equal Status, was likewise a scholar to the Crown Prince; the two were very close friends.

sentences.zh: 臻住城南，訥住城東，臻嘗欲尋訥，謂從者曰：「汝知劉儀同家乎？」

translations.literal: Zhen lived in the south of the city, Ne lived in the east of the city. Zhen once wished to visit Ne and said to his attendants: "Do you know the home of Commissioner Liu?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen lived in the south of the city and Ne in the east. Once when Zhen wished to visit Ne, he asked his attendants, "Do you know where Commissioner Liu lives?

sentences.zh: 從者不知尋訥，謂臻還家，答曰：「知。」

translations.literal: The attendants, not knowing he sought Ne, thought Zhen was returning home, and answered: "We know."
translations.idiomatic: The attendants, not realizing he meant Liu Ne, assumed he was going home and answered, "We do."

sentences.zh: 於是引之而去，既扣門，臻尚未悟，謂至訥家。

translations.literal: Thereupon they led him away; when they knocked at the door, Zhen had still not realized and thought he had arrived at Ne's home.
translations.idiomatic: So they led him off; when they knocked at a door, Zhen still did not realize his mistake and thought he had reached Ne's house.

sentences.zh: 乃據鞍大呼曰：「劉儀同可出矣。」

translations.literal: He then leaned on his saddle and shouted loudly: "Commissioner Liu, you may come out now.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on his saddle and shouted, "Commissioner Liu, come out!

sentences.zh: 其子迎門，臻驚曰：「此汝亦來耶？」

translations.literal: His son greeted him at the door; Zhen said in surprise: "You came here too?"
translations.idiomatic: His son came to the door; Zhen exclaimed in surprise, "You came here too?"

sentences.zh: 其子答曰：「此是大人家。」

translations.literal: His son answered: "This is the great man's home."
translations.idiomatic: His son replied, "This is our home, Father."

sentences.zh: 於是顧盼，久之乃悟，叱從者曰：「汝大無意，吾欲造劉訥耳。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he looked around, and after a long while finally understood; he scolded his attendants: "You were utterly without sense — I wanted to visit Liu Ne."
translations.idiomatic: He looked about, and only after a long moment understood; he scolded his attendants, "You had no idea what I meant — I wanted to visit Liu Ne!"

sentences.zh: 性好啖蜆，以音同父諱，呼為扁螺。

translations.literal: He was fond of eating freshwater clams; because the sound was the same as his father's taboo name, he called them "flat spiral shells."
translations.idiomatic: He loved eating freshwater clams, but because the word sounded like his father's taboo name, he called them "flat spiral shells."

sentences.zh: 其疏放多此類也。

translations.literal: His unrestrained conduct had many cases of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His eccentric habits were mostly of this kind.

sentences.zh: 精於《兩漢書》，時人稱為漢聖。

translations.literal: He was expert in the two Han Histories; people of the time called him "Saint of Han."
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of the two Han Histories, and his contemporaries called him the Sage of Han.

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: He died in the eighteenth year of Kaihuang, at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of Kaihuang at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection in ten volumes circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of his writings in ten volumes circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 王頍，字景文，齊州刺史頒之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang E, courtesy name Jingwen, was the younger brother of Wang Bin, Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, styled Jingwen, was the younger brother of Wang Bin, who served as Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 年數歲，值江陵陷，隨諸兄入關。

translations.literal: When a few years old, he was present when Jiangling fell and entered the pass with his elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When he was still a child, Jiangling fell; he entered the pass with his elder brothers.

sentences.zh: 少好遊俠，年二十，尚不知書。

translations.literal: In youth he loved roaming and knight-errantry; at twenty he still did not know books.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved roaming and adventure; at twenty he could scarcely read.

sentences.zh: 為其兄顒所責怒，於是感激，始讀《孝經》、《論語》，盡夜不倦。

translations.literal: Being scolded and angered by his elder brother Yong, he was stirred to zeal and began reading the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, through the whole night without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Scolded harshly by his elder brother Yong, he was stung to shame and began reading the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, studying through the night without rest.

sentences.zh: 遂讀《左傳》、《禮》、《易》、《詩》、《書》，乃歎曰：「書無不可讀者！」

translations.literal: He then read the Zuo Commentary, the Rites, the Changes, the Odes, and the Documents, and sighed: "There is no book that cannot be read!
translations.idiomatic: He went on to the Zuo Commentary, the Rites, the Changes, the Odes, and the Documents, and exclaimed, "There is no book worth refusing!

sentences.zh: 勤學累載，遂遍通五經，究其旨趣，大為儒者所稱。

translations.literal: Studying diligently for many years, he then mastered all five classics thoroughly, investigating their aims and purports, and was greatly praised by Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: After years of diligent study he mastered all five classics and grasped their deeper meaning, winning high praise from Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 解綴文，善談論。

translations.literal: He understood composition and was skilled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose prose and was skilled in debate.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，周武帝引為露門學士。

translations.literal: At twenty-two, Emperor Wu of Zhou brought him in as a Lumen Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two he was brought into service by Emperor Wu of Zhou as a Lumen Scholar.

sentences.zh: 每有疑決，多頍所為。

translations.literal: Whenever there were doubtful decisions, most were resolved by E.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever difficult questions arose, it was usually E who resolved them.

sentences.zh: 而頍性識甄明，精力不倦，好讀諸子，偏記異書，當代稱為博物。

translations.literal: Yet E's nature was discerning and clear, his energy never weary; he loved reading the masters and especially remembered unusual books; his contemporaries called him widely learned.
translations.idiomatic: E was sharp and clear-minded, tireless in energy; he loved reading the masters and had a special gift for remembering rare books, and his contemporaries called him a man of encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 又曉兵法，益有縱橫之志，每歎不逢時，常以將相自許。

translations.literal: He also understood military strategy and increasingly had ambitions of political maneuvering; he often sighed that he did not meet the right time, and frequently regarded himself as fit for general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: He also understood military strategy and grew ever more ambitious for political mastery; he often lamented that the times had not favored him and regarded himself as fit for the roles of general and minister.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Assistant Editor in the Bureau of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Kaihuang reign he received appointment as Assistant Editor in the Bureau of Documents.

sentences.zh: 尋令于國子講授。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to lecture at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was assigned to lecture at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會高祖親臨釋奠，國子祭酒元善講《孝經》，頍與相論難，詞義鋒起，善往往見屈。

translations.literal: When Gaozu personally attended the sacrifice to Confucius, Academician Yuan Shan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; E debated with him, arguments rising sharp; Shan was often put in the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu personally attended the Confucian sacrifice, Academician Yuan Shan lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; E engaged him in debate, their arguments flashing like blades, and Shan was often bested.

sentences.zh: 高祖大奇之，超授國子博士。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly struck and promoted him directly to Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly impressed and promoted him directly to Doctor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 後坐事解職，配防嶺南。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed from office for an offense and assigned to guard duty in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was dismissed from office for an offense and sent to serve guard duty in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 數載，授漢王諒府諮議參軍，王甚禮之。

translations.literal: After several years he was appointed Consultant to Prince of Han Liang's staff; the prince treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed Consultant on the staff of Prince Liang of Han, who treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 時諒見房陵及秦、蜀二王相次廢黜，潛有異志。

translations.literal: At that time Liang saw that the Princes of Fangling and of Qin and Shu were successively deposed, and secretly harbored rebellious intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang saw the Princes of Fangling, Qin, and Shu deposed one after another and secretly harbored rebellious ambitions.

sentences.zh: 頍遂陰勸諒繕治兵甲。

translations.literal: E then secretly urged Liang to repair and prepare armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: E then secretly urged Liang to gather and prepare arms.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，諒遂舉兵反，多頍之計也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Liang thereupon raised troops in rebellion — mostly E's plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu died, Liang raised troops in rebellion — largely on E's counsel.

sentences.zh: 頍後數進奇策，諒不能用。

translations.literal: E later submitted several ingenious stratagems, but Liang could not employ them.
translations.idiomatic: E later offered several ingenious stratagems, but Liang would not follow them.

sentences.zh: 楊素至蒿澤，將戰，頍謂其子曰：「氣候殊不佳，兵必敗。

translations.literal: When Yang Su reached Haohao Marsh and was about to fight, E said to his son: "The weather is extremely unfavorable; the army will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su reached Haohao Marsh and battle was imminent, E said to his son, "The signs are very bad — the army will surely be defeated.

sentences.zh: 汝可隨從我。」

translations.literal: You may follow me.
translations.idiomatic: Come with me.

sentences.zh: 既而兵敗，頍將歸突厥，至山中，徑路斷絕，知必不免，謂其子曰：「吾之計數，不減楊素，但坐言不見從，遂至於此。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the army was defeated; E was about to flee to the Turks; reaching the mountains, the path was cut off; knowing he could not escape, he said to his son: "My stratagems are no less than Yang Su's, but because I sat and spoke yet was not followed, it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the army was defeated; E tried to flee to the Turks, but in the mountains the path was cut off. Knowing he could not escape, he told his son, "My plans were no worse than Yang Su's — but because I spoke and was not heeded, it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 不能坐受擒執，以成豎子名也。

translations.literal: I cannot sit and accept capture, to make a name for a base fellow.
translations.idiomatic: I will not sit here and be captured, to become some base fellow's trophy.

sentences.zh: 吾死之後，汝慎勿過親故。」

translations.literal: After I die, you must carefully not visit relatives and friends."
translations.idiomatic: After I am dead, you must not go near any relatives or friends."

sentences.zh: 於是自殺，瘞之石窟中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself and was buried in a stone cave.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed himself, and his body was buried in a stone cave.

sentences.zh: 其子數日不得食，遂過其故人，竟為所擒。

translations.literal: His son went several days without food, then visited an old friend and was ultimately captured by him.
translations.idiomatic: His son went several days without food, then visited an old friend and was captured.

sentences.zh: 楊素求頍屍，得之，斬首，梟於太原。

translations.literal: Yang Su sought E's corpse, obtained it, beheaded it, and displayed the head at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su searched for E's body, found it, beheaded it, and displayed the head at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時年五十四。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 撰《五經大義》三十卷，有集十卷，並因兵亂，無複存者。

translations.literal: He compiled thirty fascicles of Great Meaning of the Five Classics and had a collection in ten fascicles; all were lost due to military chaos.
translations.idiomatic: He had compiled thirty fascicles of Great Meaning of the Five Classics and a collection in ten fascicles, but all were lost in the turmoil of war.

sentences.zh: 崔儦，字岐叔，清河武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Bi, courtesy name Qishu, was a native of Wucheng in Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bi, styled Qishu, came from Wucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖休，魏青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiu was Qingzhou Inspector under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiu served as Qingzhou Inspector under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父仲文，齊高陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Zhongwen was Administrator of Gaoyang under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongwen served as Administrator of Gaoyang under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 世為著姓。

translations.literal: For generations the family was a prominent clan.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had been a distinguished clan.

sentences.zh: 儦年十六，太守請為功曹，不就。

translations.literal: At sixteen Bi was invited by the Administrator to serve as Assistant Officer but declined.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen the local Administrator invited him to serve as Assistant Officer, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 少與范陽盧思道、隴西辛德源同志友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was of like mind and friendly with Lu Sixian of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close friends and kindred spirits with Lu Sixian of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 每以讀書為務，負恃才地，忽略世人。

translations.literal: He always made reading his task, relying on his talent and position, disdaining ordinary people.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to reading, trusting in his talent and family standing, and looked down on ordinary people.

sentences.zh: 大署其戶曰：「不讀五千卷書者，無得入此室。」

translations.literal: He wrote largely on his door: "Whoever has not read five thousand volumes — do not enter this room.
translations.idiomatic: He posted a large notice on his door: "Let no one who has not read five thousand volumes enter this room.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，遂博覽群言，多所通涉。

translations.literal: Within a few years he then broadly read many works and mastered much.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had read widely across many fields and mastered a great deal.

sentences.zh: 解屬文，在齊舉秀才，為員外散騎侍郎，遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He understood prose composition; under Qi he was recommended as xiucai, served as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and was transferred to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in prose composition, he was recommended as a xiucai under Qi, served as Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and was later transferred to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 尋與熊安生、馬敬德等議《五禮》，兼修律令。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined Xiong Ansheng, Ma Jingde, and others in deliberating on the Five Rites, and also helped revise statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined Xiong Ansheng, Ma Jingde, and others in deliberating on the Five Rites and also helped revise statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 尋兼散騎侍郎，聘于陳。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he additionally served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and was sent as envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and sent as envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 使還，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Returning from his mission, he waited for edicts at the Wulin Library.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, he awaited imperial orders at the Wulin Library.

sentences.zh: 曆殿中、膳部、員外三曹郎中。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director in the Bureau of Palace Affairs, Bureau of Revenues, and Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director in the Bureaus of Palace Affairs, Revenues, and Appointments.

sentences.zh: 儦與頓丘李若俱見稱重，時人為之語曰：「京師灼灼，崔儦、李若。」

translations.literal: Bi and Li Ruo of Dunqiu were both seen and highly esteemed; people of the time made a saying for them: "In the capital, blazing bright — Cui Bi and Li Ruo.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and Li Ruo of Dunqiu were both held in high esteem; people of the time coined a saying: "In the capital, shining bright — Cui Bi and Li Ruo.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，歸鄉里，仕郡為功曹，州補主簿。

translations.literal: When Qi perished, he returned to his hometown, served the commandery as Assistant Officer, and was supplemented by the province as Chief Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell, he returned to his hometown, served the commandery as Assistant Officer, and was appointed Chief Recorder by the province.

sentences.zh: 開皇四年，征授給事郎，尋兼內史舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaihuang he was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Regular Service, and soon additionally served as Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaihuang he was summoned and appointed Attendant-in-Regular Service, and soon additionally served as Palace Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後數年，兼通直散騎侍郎，聘于陳，還授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Several years later he additionally served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalier Office, was sent as envoy to Chen, and on return was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he additionally served as Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Cavalier Office, was sent as envoy to Chen, and on returning was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 越國公楊素時方貴幸，重儦門地，為子玄縱娶其女為妻。

translations.literal: Duke of Yue Yang Su was then just at the height of favor; he valued Bi's family standing and had his son Xuanyong marry Bi's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yue Yang Su was then at the height of imperial favor; he valued Bi's family standing and had his son Xuanyong marry Bi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 聘禮甚厚。

translations.literal: The betrothal gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The betrothal gifts were exceedingly generous.

sentences.zh: 親迎之始，公卿滿座，素令騎迎儦，亻麃故敝其衣冠，騎驢而至。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the formal welcome, ministers and officials filled the seats; Su ordered a rider to fetch Bi — Bi deliberately wore tattered clothes and cap and arrived riding a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the formal welcome, when ministers and officials filled the hall, Su sent a rider to fetch Bi — who deliberately wore shabby clothes and arrived riding a donkey.

sentences.zh: 素推令上座，儦有輕素之色，禮甚倨，言又不遜。

translations.literal: Su pushed him to the upper seat, but Bi showed a look of contempt for Su; his courtesy was very arrogant and his words also insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed him to the seat of honor, but Bi showed open contempt; his bearing was haughty and his words insolent.

sentences.zh: 素忿然，拂衣而起，竟罷座。

translations.literal: Su angrily swept his robes and rose; in the end the banquet was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Su flushed with anger, swept from his seat, and the banquet was broken up entirely.

sentences.zh: 後數日，儦方來謝，素待之如初。

translations.literal: Several days later Bi finally came to apologize; Su treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Bi finally came to apologize, and Su treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，卒于京師，時年七十二。

translations.literal: During Renshou he died in the capital, at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he died in the capital at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子世濟。

translations.literal: His son was Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shiji.

sentences.zh: 諸葛潁，字漢，丹陽建康人也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ying, courtesy name Han, was a native of Jiankang in Danyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ying, courtesy name Han, was a native of Jiankang in Danyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖銓，梁零陵太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Administrator of Lingling under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan served as Administrator of Lingling under the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 父規，義陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui served as Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 潁年八歲，能屬文，起家梁邵陵王參軍事，轉記室。

translations.literal: At eight Ying could compose prose; he began his career as Aide to Prince Shaoling of Liang and was transferred to Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could compose prose; he began his career as Aide to Prince Shaoling of Liang and was later transferred to Recorder.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，奔齊，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: During Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Qi and awaited edicts at the Wulin Library.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Qi and awaited imperial orders at the Wulin Library.

sentences.zh: 曆太學博士、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He served successively as Doctor of the Imperial Academy and Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Doctor of the Imperial Academy and Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，不得調，杜門不出者十餘年。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he received no appointment and shut his doors, not going out for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he received no appointment and shut his doors, not venturing out for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 習《周易》、圖緯、《倉》、《雅》、《莊》、《老》，頗得其要。

translations.literal: He studied the Book of Changes, apocryphal texts, the Cangjie, the Erya, Zhuangzi, and Laozi, and rather grasped their essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Book of Changes, apocryphal texts, the Cangjie Primer, the Erya, Zhuangzi, and Laozi, and grasped their essentials rather well.

sentences.zh: 清辨有俊才，晉王廣素聞其名，引為參軍事，轉記室。

translations.literal: Clear in debate and possessing outstanding talent, Prince of Jin Guang had long heard his name and brought him in as Aide, then transferred him to Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Clear in debate and gifted with outstanding talent, Prince of Jin Yang Guang had long heard his name and brought him in as Aide, then transferred him to Recorder.

sentences.zh: 及王為太子，除藥藏監。

translations.literal: When the prince became Crown Prince, he was appointed Director of the Medical Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became Crown Prince, he was appointed Director of the Medical Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷著作郎，甚見親幸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was transferred to Editing Clerk and was greatly seen and favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was transferred to Editing Clerk and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 出入臥內，帝每賜之曲宴，輒與皇后嬪禦連席共榻。

translations.literal: He went in and out of the bedchamber; the emperor often granted him private banquets, and he would share mat and seat with the empress and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: He went in and out of the imperial bedchamber; the emperor often granted him private banquets, and he would share mat and seat with the empress and her attendants.

sentences.zh: 潁因間隙，多所譖毀，是以時人謂之「冶葛」。

translations.literal: Ying used openings to slander and destroy many; therefore people of the time called him "Refined Kudzu."
translations.idiomatic: Ying used every opening to slander others, so people of the time called him "Refined Kudzu" — a poisonous vine.

sentences.zh: 後錄恩舊，授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Later, when old benefactors were recorded, he was granted Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when old benefactors were rewarded, he was granted the title Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 帝常賜潁詩，其卒章曰：「參翰長洲苑，侍講肅成門。

translations.literal: The emperor often bestowed poems on Ying; the closing stanza reads: "Joining the brush at Changzhou Garden, lecturing beside the throne at Suicheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often bestowed poems on Ying; the closing lines read: "At Changzhou Garden you joined the brush; at Suicheng Gate you lectured beside the throne.

sentences.zh: 名理窮研核，英華恣討論。

translations.literal: Name and principle exhaustively examined and verified; flowering brilliance freely debated.
translations.idiomatic: You exhaustively examined name and principle; you freely debated flowering brilliance.

sentences.zh: 實錄資平允，傳芳導後昆。」

translations.literal: True records rely on fairness and balance; passing fragrance guides later generations.
translations.idiomatic: True records rely on fair judgment; passing fragrance guides posterity.

sentences.zh: 其見待遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the treatment he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the treatment he received.

sentences.zh: 後征吐谷渾，加正議大夫。

translations.literal: Later when campaigning against Tuyuhun, he was given the additional title Regular Grand Master for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the army marched against Tuyuhun, he was given the additional title Regular Grand Master for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 後從駕北巡，卒於道，年七十七。

translations.literal: Later he accompanied the imperial carriage on the northern tour and died on the road, at age seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor on the northern tour and died on the road at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 潁性褊急，與柳抃每相忿鬩，帝屢責怒之而猶不止，於後帝亦薄之。

translations.literal: Ying's nature was narrow and quick-tempered; he and Liu Bian constantly quarreled in anger; the emperor repeatedly scolded and rebuked them yet they still did not stop; afterward the emperor also grew cold toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was narrow and quick-tempered; he and Liu Bian constantly quarreled. The emperor repeatedly scolded them but they would not stop; afterward the emperor also grew cool toward him.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，撰《鑾駕北巡記》三卷，《幸江都道裡記》一卷，《洛陽古今記》一卷，《馬名錄》二卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collection in twenty fascicles and compiled Record of the Imperial Carriage's Northern Tour in three fascicles, Record of the Route to Jiangdu in one fascicle, Record of Luoyang Past and Present in one fascicle, and Register of Horse Names in two fascicles — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection in twenty fascicles and compiled Record of the Imperial Carriage's Northern Tour in three fascicles, Record of the Route to Jiangdu in one fascicle, Record of Luoyang Past and Present in one fascicle, and Register of Horse Names in two fascicles — all circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 有子嘉會。

translations.literal: He had a son Jiahui.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Jiahui.

sentences.zh: 孫萬壽，字仙期，信都武強人也。

translations.literal: Sun Wanshou, courtesy name Xianqi, was a native of Wuqiang in Xindu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wanshou, courtesy name Xianqi, was a native of Wuqiang in Xindu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖寶，魏散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bao was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bao served as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary under Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父靈暉，齊國子博士。

translations.literal: His father Linghui was Doctor of the Imperial Academy under Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linghui served as Doctor of the Imperial Academy under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 萬壽年十四，就阜城熊安生受五經，略通大義，兼博涉子史。

translations.literal: At fourteen Wanshou studied the Five Classics under Xiong Ansheng of Fucheng, gaining a general grasp of their great meaning while also reading broadly in masters and histories.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Wanshou studied the Five Classics under Xiong Ansheng of Fucheng, gaining a general grasp of their meaning while also reading widely in masters and histories.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，美談笑，博陵李德林見而奇之。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing prose, graceful in conversation and laughter — Li Delin of Boling saw him and was struck.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at composition and gracious in conversation, he astonished Li Delin of Boling when they met.

sentences.zh: 在齊，年十七，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Under Qi, at seventeen he served as Court Gentleman for Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi, at seventeen he served as Court Gentleman for Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，滕穆王引為文學，坐衣冠不整，配防江南。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Prince Teng the Valiant brought him in as Literary Scholar; for improper dress he was assigned to guard duty in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu accepted the abdication, Prince Teng the Valiant brought him in as Literary Scholar; for improper dress he was assigned to guard duty in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 行軍總管宇文述召典軍書。

translations.literal: Campaign Commander Yuwen Shu summoned him to manage military documents.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign Commander Yuwen Shu summoned him to manage military documents.

sentences.zh: 萬壽本自書生，從容文雅，一旦從軍，鬱鬱不得志，為五言詩贈京邑知友曰：

translations.literal: Wanshou was originally a scholar, easy and refined — but thrust overnight into military service, he grew depressed and unfulfilled, and composed a pentasyllabic poem to send to his friends in the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou had been a scholar, easy and refined — but thrust overnight into military service, he grew depressed and unfulfilled, and composed a pentasyllabic poem to send to his friends in the capital:

sentences.zh: 賈誼長沙國，屈平湘水濱。

translations.literal: Jia Yi [served in] the kingdom of Changsha; Qu Ping [dwelt by] the banks of the Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi served in the kingdom of Changsha; Qu Ping dwelt by the banks of the Xiang.

sentences.zh: 江南瘴癘地，從來多逐臣。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan region is a land of miasma and pestilence — from old it has held many exiled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan region is a land of miasma and pestilence — from of old it has held many exiled ministers.

sentences.zh: 粵餘非巧宦，少小拙謀身。

translations.literal: As for me, I am no skilled courtier; from youth I have been clumsy at managing my own affairs.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I am no skilled courtier; from youth I have been clumsy at managing my own affairs.

sentences.zh: 欲飛無假翼，思鳴不值晨。

translations.literal: I wish to fly but have no borrowed wings; I yearn to sing but find no dawn to greet me.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to fly but have no wings to borrow; I yearn to sing but find no dawn to greet me.

sentences.zh: 如何載筆士，翻作負戈人！

translations.literal: How is it that a man who bears the writing brush has turned into one who carries a spear!
translations.idiomatic: How is it that a man who bears the writing brush has turned into one who carries a spear!

sentences.zh: 飄飄如木偶，棄置同凶狗。

translations.literal: Drifting like a wooden puppet, cast aside like a vicious dog.
translations.idiomatic: Drifting like a wooden puppet, cast aside like a vicious dog.

sentences.zh: 失路乃西浮，非狂亦東走。

translations.literal: Losing my way I drift westward; not mad, yet I run east as well.
translations.idiomatic: Losing my way I drift westward; not mad, yet I run east as well.

sentences.zh: 晚歲出函關，方春度京口。

translations.literal: In late years I passed out through Hangu Pass; in early spring I crossed Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In late years I passed out through Hangu Pass; in early spring I crossed Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 石城臨獸據，天津望牛鬥。

translations.literal: From Stone City I looked toward Beast Perch; from Heavenly Ford I gazed at Ox and Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: From Stone City I looked toward Beast Perch; from Heavenly Ford I gazed at Ox and Dipper.

sentences.zh: 牛鬥盛妖氛，梟獍已成群。

translations.literal: Ox and Dipper swelled with baleful vapors; owls and jackals had already formed packs.
translations.idiomatic: Ox and Dipper swelled with baleful vapors; owls and jackals had already formed packs.

sentences.zh: 郗超初入幕，王粲始從軍。

translations.literal: Xi Chao first entered the staff; Wang Can first joined the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao first entered the staff; Wang Can first joined the army.

sentences.zh: 裹糧楚山際，被甲吳江汶。

translations.literal: We packed rations at the foot of Chu mountains; we donned armor along the Wu river banks.
translations.idiomatic: We packed rations at the foot of Chu mountains; we donned armor along the Wu river banks.

sentences.zh: 吳江一浩蕩，楚山何糾紛。

translations.literal: The Wu river — one vast flood; the Chu mountains — how tangled and confused!
translations.idiomatic: The Wu river — one vast flood; the Chu mountains — how tangled and confused!

sentences.zh: 驚波上濺日，喬木下臨雲。

translations.literal: Startled waves splashed the sun from below; tall trees hung clouds beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: Startled waves splashed the sun from below; tall trees hung clouds beneath them.

sentences.zh: 擊越恆資辯，喻蜀幾飛文。

translations.literal: Quelling Yue always relied on eloquence; instructing Shu nearly took flight in prose.
translations.idiomatic: Quelling Yue always relied on eloquence; instructing Shu nearly took flight in prose.

sentences.zh: 魯連唯救患，吾彥不爭勳。

translations.literal: Lu Liang alone wished to relieve distress; Wu Yan refused to compete for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Liang alone wished to relieve distress; Wu Yan refused to compete for merit.

sentences.zh: 羈遊歲月久，歸思常搔首。

translations.literal: Long months of wandering abroad — thoughts of home constantly make me wring my hands.
translations.idiomatic: Long months of wandering abroad — thoughts of home constantly make me wring my hands.

sentences.zh: 非關不樹萱，豈為無杯酒！

translations.literal: It is not that I neglect to plant daylilies; nor is it for lack of a cup of wine!
translations.idiomatic: It is not that I neglect to plant daylilies; nor is it for lack of a cup of wine!

sentences.zh: 數載辭鄉縣，三秋別親友。

translations.literal: For years I have been away from home; for three autumns I have parted from kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: For years I have been away from home; for three autumns I have parted from kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 壯志後風雲，衰鬢先蒲柳。

translations.literal: My soaring ambitions lag behind the winds and clouds; my fading temples race ahead of the reed and willow.
translations.idiomatic: My soaring ambitions lag behind the winds and clouds; my fading temples race ahead of the reed and willow.

sentences.zh: 心緒亂如絲，空懷疇昔時。

translations.literal: My thoughts tangle like silk threads; in vain I cherish days gone by.
translations.idiomatic: My thoughts tangle like silk threads; in vain I cherish days gone by.

sentences.zh: 昔時遊帝裡，弱歲逢知己。

translations.literal: In days past I wandered the imperial capital; in youth I met kindred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In days past I wandered the imperial capital; in youth I met kindred spirits.

sentences.zh: 旅食南館中，飛蓋西園裡。

translations.literal: Boarding at the southern lodge, riding with raised canopies in the western garden.
translations.idiomatic: Boarding at the southern lodge, riding with raised canopies in the western garden.

sentences.zh: 河間本好書，東平唯愛士。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian had always loved books; the Prince of Dongping cherished scholars alone.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Hejian had always loved books; the Prince of Dongping cherished scholars alone.

sentences.zh: 英辯接天人，清言洞名理。

translations.literal: Eloquent brilliance joined heaven and earth; pure discourse penetrated name and principle.
translations.idiomatic: Eloquent brilliance joined heaven and earth; pure discourse penetrated name and principle.

sentences.zh: 鳳池時寓直，麟閣常遊止。

translations.literal: At Phoenix Pool I sometimes lodged on duty; at Unicorn Pavilion I often wandered and rested.
translations.idiomatic: At Phoenix Pool I sometimes lodged on duty; at Unicorn Pavilion I often wandered and rested.

sentences.zh: 勝地盛賓僚，麗景相攜招。

translations.literal: In splendid places guests and colleagues gathered; in beautiful scenes we called one another forth.
translations.idiomatic: In splendid places guests and colleagues gathered; in beautiful scenes we called one another forth.

sentences.zh: 舟泛昆明水，騎指渭津橋。

translations.literal: Boats drifted on Kunming Lake; riders pointed toward Wei Ford Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Boats drifted on Kunming Lake; riders pointed toward Wei Ford Bridge.

sentences.zh: 祓除臨灞岸，供帳出東郊。

translations.literal: Spring purification beside Ba banks; feast pavilions pitched beyond the eastern wall.
translations.idiomatic: Spring purification beside the Ba banks; feast pavilions pitched beyond the eastern wall.

sentences.zh: 宜城醖始熟，陽翟曲新調。

translations.literal: Yicheng wine just ripened; Yangdi tunes freshly arranged.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng wine had just ripened; Yangdi tunes were freshly arranged.

sentences.zh: 繞樹烏啼夜，雊麥雉飛朝。

translations.literal: At night crows called around the trees; at dawn pheasants flew calling among the wheat.
translations.idiomatic: At night crows called around the trees; at dawn pheasants flew calling among the wheat.

sentences.zh: 細塵梁下落，長袖掌中嬌。

translations.literal: Fine dust fell beneath the beams; long sleeves and palms held their delicate charms.
translations.idiomatic: Fine dust fell beneath the beams; long sleeves and palms held their delicate charms.

sentences.zh: 歡娛三樂至，懷抱百憂銷。

translations.literal: Three joys of pleasure arrived; the hundred cares in my breast dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Three joys of pleasure arrived; the hundred cares in my breast dissolved.

sentences.zh: 夢想猶如昨，尋思久寂寥。

translations.literal: Dreams seem still like yesterday; yet long brooding brings only desolation.
translations.idiomatic: Dreams seem still like yesterday; yet long brooding brings only desolation.

sentences.zh: 一朝牽世網，萬里逐波潮。

translations.literal: In a single morning the world's net drew me in; ten thousand leagues I chase the tide.
translations.idiomatic: In a single morning the world's net drew me in; ten thousand leagues I chase the tide.

sentences.zh: 回輪常自轉，懸旆不堪搖。

translations.literal: Wheels constantly turn on their own; the hanging banners cannot bear to be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Wheels constantly turn on their own; the hanging banners cannot bear to be shaken.

sentences.zh: 登高視衿帶，鄉關白雲外。

translations.literal: Climbing high I gaze at belt and stream; my homeland lies beyond the white clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Climbing high I gaze at belt and stream; my homeland lies beyond the white clouds.

sentences.zh: 回首望孤城，愁人益不平。

translations.literal: Turning back I look upon the lonely city; the troubled man grows ever more restless.
translations.idiomatic: Turning back I look upon the lonely city; the troubled man grows ever more restless.

sentences.zh: 華亭宵鶴唳，幽谷早鶯鳴。

translations.literal: At night cranes cry from Huating Pavilion; at dawn orioles sing in the hidden valley.
translations.idiomatic: At night cranes cry from Huating Pavilion; at dawn orioles sing in the hidden valley.

sentences.zh: 斷絕心難續，惝恍魂屢驚。

translations.literal: Severed connections — the heart cannot continue; dim and dazed, the soul is shaken again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Severed connections — the heart cannot continue; dim and dazed, the soul is shaken again and again.

sentences.zh: 群紀通家好，鄒魯故鄉情。

translations.literal: The Ji clan and others were family friends; Zou and Lu hold the feelings of my native place.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji clan and others were family friends; Zou and Lu hold the feelings of my native place.

sentences.zh: 若值南飛雁，時能訪死生。

translations.literal: If you meet the wild geese flying south, from time to time inquire after my life and death.
translations.idiomatic: If you meet the wild geese flying south, from time to time inquire after my life and death.

sentences.zh: 此詩至京，盛為當時之所吟誦，天下好事者多書壁而玩之。

translations.literal: When this poem reached the capital it was greatly chanted by those of the time; lovers of fine things throughout the realm often copied it on walls and treasured it.
translations.idiomatic: When this poem reached the capital it was widely chanted in its day; lovers of fine things throughout the realm copied it on walls and treasured it.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，十餘年不得調。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his hometown and for more than ten years received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to his hometown and for more than ten years received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，征拜豫章王長史，非其好也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was summoned and appointed Chief of Staff to the Prince of Yuzhang — not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renshou he was summoned and appointed Chief of Staff to the Prince of Yuzhang — not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 王轉封于齊，即為齊王文學。

translations.literal: When the prince was transferred and enfeoffed in Qi, he became Literary Scholar to the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was transferred and enfeoffed in Qi, Wanshou became Literary Scholar to the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 當時諸王官屬多被夷滅，由是彌不自安，因謝病免。

translations.literal: At that time many staff members of the princes were executed; accordingly he grew ever more uneasy and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many staff members of the princes were executed; accordingly he grew ever more uneasy and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，授大理司直，卒于官，時年五十二。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Judicial Inspector of the Court of Review and died in office, at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was appointed Judicial Inspector of the Court of Review and died in office at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collection in ten fascicles circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection in ten fascicles circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 王貞，字孝逸，梁郡東留人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, courtesy name Xiaoyi, was a native of Dongliu in Liang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, courtesy name Xiaoyi, was a native of Dongliu in Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，七歲好學，善《毛詩》、《禮記》、《左氏傳》、《周易》，諸子百家，無不畢覽。

translations.literal: As a youth he was clever and quick; at seven he loved learning, excelling in the Mao Odes, the Record of Rites, the Zuo Commentary, and the Book of Changes — of the masters and the hundred schools there was none he did not read through.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and quick; at seven he loved learning, excelling in the Mao Odes, the Record of Rites, the Zuo Commentary, and the Book of Changes — of the masters and the hundred schools there was none he did not read through.

sentences.zh: 善屬文詞，不治產業，每以諷讀為娛。

translations.literal: Skilled at literary composition, he did not manage family estates and took recitation and reading as his recreation.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at literary composition, he did not manage family estates and took recitation and reading as his recreation.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，汴州刺史樊叔略引為主簿，後舉秀才，授縣尉，非其好也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Fan Shulue, Governor of Bian province, brought him in as Chief Recorder; later recommended as xiucai, he was appointed County Commandant — not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Fan Shulue, Governor of Bian province, brought him in as Chief Recorder; later recommended as xiucai, he was appointed County Commandant — not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 謝病於家。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and remained at home.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，齊王暕鎮江都，聞其名，以書召之曰：

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Prince of Qi Yang Jian was stationed at Jiangdu; hearing Zhen's name, he summoned him by letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Prince of Qi Yang Jian was stationed at Jiangdu; hearing Zhen's name, he summoned him by letter, saying:

sentences.zh: 夫山藏美玉，光照廊廡之間，地蘊神劍，氣浮星漢之表。

translations.literal: Mountains hide fine jade whose light shines between corridor and eaves; earth holds divine swords whose spirit rises above the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains hide fine jade whose radiance shines between corridor and eaves; earth holds divine swords whose spirit rises above the Milky Way.

sentences.zh: 是知毛遂穎脫，義感平原，孫慧文詞，來遷東海。

translations.literal: Knowing this — Mao Sui's tapered awl breaking through its sheath moved Lord Pingyuan by righteousness; Sun Hui's literary compositions brought him to transfer to Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we know that when Mao Sui's tapered awl broke through its sheath, he moved Lord Pingyuan by righteousness; when Sun Hui's literary skill shone forth, he was transferred to Donghai.

sentences.zh: 顧循寡薄，有懷髦彥，籍甚清風，為日久矣，未獲披覿，良深佇遲。

translations.literal: Looking back, I am meager and slight, yet I harbor admiration for eminent talents; your outstanding reputation has been long-standing; I have not yet obtained a face-to-face meeting — my longing is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back, I am meager and slight, yet I harbor admiration for eminent talents; your outstanding reputation has long preceded you, and I have not yet had the honor of meeting you face to face — my longing runs very deep indeed.

sentences.zh: 比高天流火，早應涼飆，陵雲仙掌，方承清露，想攝衛攸宜，與時休適。

translations.literal: Now that the High Heaven's flowing fire has early responded to the cool wind, and Lingyun's Immortal Palm is just receiving clear dew, I imagine your regimen is as it should be and accords with the season's comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the High Heaven's flowing fire has already yielded to the cool wind, and Lingyun's Immortal Palm is just receiving clear dew, I trust your regimen is as it should be and that you are at ease with the season.

sentences.zh: 前園後圃，從容丘壑之情，左琴右書，蕭散煙霞之外。

translations.literal: Garden in front, orchard behind — the ease of hills and ravines; lute to the left, books to the right — carefree beyond mist and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: With a garden before you and an orchard behind, you enjoy the ease of hills and ravines; with a lute to your left and books to your right, you roam carefree beyond mist and clouds.

sentences.zh: 茂陵謝病，非無《封禪》之文，彭澤遺榮，先有《歸來》之作。

translations.literal: At Maoling he declined on grounds of illness — not that he lacked his rhapsody on the Feng and Shan; at Pengze he abandoned glory — he had already composed his "Homecoming."
translations.idiomatic: At Maoling Sima Xiangru declined on grounds of illness — not that he lacked his rhapsody on the Feng and Shan sacrifices; at Pengze Tao Yuanming abandoned worldly glory — he had already composed his "Homecoming."

sentences.zh: 優遊儒雅，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Loitering at ease in refined elegance — what joy could surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: To roam at ease in refined learning — what joy could surpass this!

sentences.zh: 余屬當籓屏，宣條揚、越，坐棠聽訟，事絕詠歌，攀桂摛詞，眷言高遁。

translations.literal: I happen to serve as a frontier screen, promulgating laws in Yang and Yue; seated beneath the crabapple hearing lawsuits — no occasion for lyric song; I pluck cassia and compose verses, yet my heart turns to lofty retreat.
translations.idiomatic: I happen to serve as a frontier shield, promulgating laws across Yang and Yue; seated beneath the crabapple tree to hear lawsuits, I have no leisure for lyric song — yet as I pluck cassia and compose verses, my heart turns ever toward lofty retreat.

sentences.zh: 至於揚旌北渚，飛蓋西園，托乘乏應、劉，置醴闕申、穆，背淮之賓，徒聞其語，趨燕之客，罕值其人。

translations.literal: As for raising banners on the northern islet, flying canopies in the western garden — for riding companions I lack Ying and Liu; for setting out wine I miss Shen and Mu; guests from north of the Huai hear such talk but in vain; guests hurrying to Yan rarely meet their man.
translations.idiomatic: When I raise banners on the northern islet or fly canopies in the western garden, I lack Ying and Liu for riding companions and Shen and Mu to set out the wine; guests from north of the Huai hear such talk but in vain, and guests hurrying to Yan rarely meet their man.

sentences.zh: 卿道冠鷹揚，聲高鳳舉，儒墨泉海，詞章苑囿，棲遲衡泌，懷寶迷邦，徇茲獨善，良以於邑。

translations.literal: Your Way crowns the soaring hawk; your fame rises like the phoenix soaring; Confucian and Mohist learning — a spring-sea; prose and verse — a garden-park; you linger at Heng and Bi, hoarding treasure in a benighted state, pursuing solitary virtue alone — this brings me much distress.
translations.idiomatic: Your Way crowns the soaring hawk; your fame rises like the phoenix in flight; Confucian and Mohist learning fill you like a spring-sea, prose and verse like a garden-park — yet you linger at Heng and Bi, hoarding treasure in a benighted state and pursuing solitary virtue alone. This fills me with distress.

sentences.zh: 今遣行人，具宣往意，側望起予，甚於饑渴，想便輕舉，副此虛心。

translations.literal: Now I send a messenger to fully convey my intent of summoning you; I lean and look expectantly for what will rouse me — more than hunger and thirst; I trust you will soon lightly make the journey to answer this sincere mind.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send a messenger to convey fully my intent to summon you; I lean and look expectantly for what will rouse me — more urgently than hunger or thirst — and trust you will soon make the journey to answer this sincere invitation.

sentences.zh: 無信投石之談，空慕鑿壞之逸，書不盡言，更慚詞費。

translations.literal: Without the credence of stone-throwing words, I merely admire in vain the leisure of Chisun Huai; writing cannot exhaust speech — I am only the more ashamed of wordiness.
translations.idiomatic: Without the credence of Zhu Ji's stone-throwing pledge, I can only admire in vain the hermit leisure of Chisun Huai; writing cannot exhaust my meaning, and I am all the more ashamed of my wordiness.

sentences.zh: 及貞至，王以客禮待之，朝夕遣問安不。

translations.literal: When Zhen arrived, the prince treated him with guest protocol, morning and evening sending to inquire after his well-being.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen arrived, the prince treated him with the courtesy due a guest, morning and evening sending to inquire after his well-being.

sentences.zh: 又索文集，貞啟謝曰：

translations.literal: The prince also requested his collected writings; Zhen submitted a letter of thanks, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The prince also requested his collected writings; Zhen submitted a memorial of thanks, saying:

sentences.zh: 屬賀德仁宣教，須少來所有拙文。

translations.literal: At the direction of He Deren, who conveyed the order, I must briefly submit the crude writings I possess.
translations.idiomatic: At the direction of He Deren, who conveyed the order, I must briefly submit the crude writings in my possession.

sentences.zh: 昔公旦之才藝，能事鬼神，夫子之文章，性與天道，雅志傳于游、夏，餘波鼓于屈、宋，雕龍之跡，具在風騷，而前賢後聖，代相師祖。

translations.literal: Formerly the Duke of Zhou's talents and arts could serve the ghosts and spirits; the Master's writings were of one nature with Heaven and Way; refined aspirations were handed down through You and Xia; aftercurrents surged in Qu and Song; the traces of the Carving Dragon are fully present in Feng and Sao — while former worthies and later sages have in each generation been each other's teachers and models.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Duke of Zhou's talents and arts could serve the ghosts and spirits; the Master's writings were of one nature with Heaven and the Way; refined aspirations were handed down through You and Xia, aftercurrents surged in Qu Yuan and Song Yu, and the traces of the Carving Dragon are fully present in the Feng and Sao — while former worthies and later sages have in each generation been one another's teachers and models.

sentences.zh: 賞逐時移，出門分路，變清音於正始，體高致于元康，鹹言坐握蛇珠，誰許獨為麟角。

translations.literal: Judgment follows the shifting times; parting at the gate each takes a different road — changing clear tones at Zhengshi, embodying lofty bearing at Yuankang; everyone says they hold the serpent pearl sitting still — who grants that one alone possesses the unicorn's horn?
translations.idiomatic: Judgment follows the shifting times; at the gate each man takes a different road — clear tones changed at Zhengshi, lofty bearing embodied at Yuankang; everyone claims to hold the serpent pearl while sitting still — who grants that one alone possesses the unicorn's horn?

sentences.zh: 孝逸生於戰爭之季，長於風塵之世，學無半古，才不逮人。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi was born in the season of warfare and grew up in a world of dust and turmoil; my learning does not reach half the ancients' and my talent falls short of others.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyi was born in an age of warfare and grew up in a world of dust and turmoil; my learning does not reach half the ancients', and my talent falls short of others.

sentences.zh: 往屬休明，寸陰已昃，雖居可封之屋，每懷貧賤之恥。

translations.literal: In former days I belonged to an age of glory, yet my daylight had already passed the west — though I dwelt in a house fit for enfeoffment, I always harbored the shame of poverty and low station.
translations.idiomatic: In former days I belonged to an age of glory, yet my daylight had already passed its zenith — though I dwelt in a house fit for enfeoffment, I always harbored the shame of poverty and low station.

sentences.zh: 適鄢郢而迷途，入邯鄲而失步，歸來反覆，心灰遂寒。

translations.literal: Going to Yan and Ying I lost my way; entering Handan I missed my step — returning again and again, my heart turned to ash and grew cold.
translations.idiomatic: Going to Yan and Ying I lost my way; entering Handan I missed my step — returning again and again, my heart turned to ash and grew cold.

sentences.zh: 豈謂橫議過實，虛塵睿覽，枉高車以載鼷，費明珠以彈雀，遂得裹糧三月，重高門之餘地，背淮千里，望章台之後塵。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that idle talk exceeded reality and falsely soiled the emperor's gaze — wrongly sending a high carriage to carry a mouse, wasting a bright pearl to shoot a sparrow — thus I packed provisions for three months and returned to the honored gate's leavings, came a thousand li from north of the Huai, and looked toward the trailing dust of Zhang Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought that exaggerated praise exceeded reality and falsely soiled the sage's gaze — sending a high carriage to carry a mouse, wasting a bright pearl to shoot a sparrow — so that I packed provisions for three months, returned to the honored gate's leavings, came a thousand li from north of the Huai, and looked toward the trailing dust of Zhang Terrace.

sentences.zh: 與懸黎而並肆，將駿驥而同阜，終朝擊缶，匪黃鐘之所諧，日暮卻行，何前人之能及！

translations.literal: To stand in the same marketplace as Hanging Categorite, to share the same hill with a swift steed — all morning striking earthen jars, not in harmony with the yellow bell; at dusk walking backward — how could I reach the men of old!
translations.idiomatic: To stand in the same marketplace as Hanging Categorite jade, to share the same hill with a swift steed — all morning striking earthen jars, not in harmony with the yellow bell; at dusk walking backward — how could I reach the men of old!

sentences.zh: 顧想平生，觸途多感，但以積年沈痼，遺忘日久，拙思所存，才成三十三卷。

translations.literal: Looking back on my whole life, every path touches many feelings — but because of chronic deep illness and long forgetting, what crude thoughts remain amount to only thirty-three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back on my whole life, every path stirs many feelings — but because of chronic deep illness and long forgetting, the crude thoughts that remain amount to only thirty-three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 仰而不至，方見學仙之遠，窺而不睹，始知遊聖之難。

translations.literal: Looking up yet not arriving — only then does one see how far it is to learn from immortals; peering yet not beholding — only then does one know how hard it is to roam in sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up yet not arriving — only then does one see how far it is to learn from immortals; peering yet not beholding — only then does one know how hard it is to roam in sagehood.

sentences.zh: 咫尺天人，周章不暇，怖甚真龍之降，慚過白豕之歸，伏紙陳情，形神悚越。

translations.literal: A mere foot or inch from heaven's man — flustered without respite; I am terrified as though a true dragon were descending, ashamed as though it were the White Boar's return; prostrate on paper I lay out my feelings, body and spirit trembling beyond bounds.
translations.idiomatic: A mere step from heaven's chosen man — flustered without respite; I am terrified as though a true dragon were descending, ashamed as though it were the White Boar's return; prostrate on paper I lay out my feelings, body and spirit trembling beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 齊王覽所上集，善之，賜良馬四匹。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi read the collection he submitted, admired it, and granted four fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi read the collection Zhen submitted, admired it, and granted four fine horses.

sentences.zh: 貞複上《江都賦》，王賜錢十萬貫，馬二匹。

translations.literal: Zhen again submitted his Rhapsody on Jiangdu; the prince granted one hundred thousand strings of cash and two horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again submitted his Rhapsody on Jiangdu; the prince granted one hundred thousand strings of cash and two horses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾甚還鄉里，終於家。

translations.literal: Before long, his illness grew severe and he returned to his hometown, dying at home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his illness grew severe; he returned to his hometown and died there.

sentences.zh: 虞綽 辛大德虞綽，字士裕，會稽余姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chuo and Xin Dade — Yu Chuo, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chuo and Xin Dade — Yu Chuo, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Yuyao in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 父孝曾，陳始興王諮議。

translations.literal: His father Xiao Zeng served as Adviser to the Prince of Shixing of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiao Zeng served as Adviser to the Prince of Shixing of Chen.

sentences.zh: 綽身長八尺，姿儀甚偉，博學有俊才，尤工草隸。

translations.literal: Chuo stood eight chi tall, with a very imposing bearing; broadly learned with outstanding talent, he was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo stood eight chi tall, with a very imposing bearing; broadly learned and gifted with outstanding talent, he was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 陳左衛將軍傅縡有盛名於世，見綽詞賦，歎謂人曰：「虞郎之文，無以尚也！」

translations.literal: Fu Zan, Left Guard General of Chen, had great fame in the world; seeing Chuo's poetry and rhapsodies, he sighed and told others: "Young Master Yu's writings cannot be surpassed!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zan, Left Guard General of Chen, enjoyed great fame in the world; seeing Chuo's poetry and rhapsodies, he sighed and told others: "Young Master Yu's writings cannot be surpassed!

sentences.zh: 仕陳為太學博士，遷永陽王記室。

translations.literal: He served Chen as Doctor of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Recorder for the Prince of Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chen as Doctor of the Imperial Academy and was transferred to Recorder for the Prince of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，晉王廣引為學士。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Prince of Jin Yang Guang brought him in as Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Prince of Jin Yang Guang brought him in as Literary Scholar.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉為秘書學士，奉詔與秘書郎虞世南、著作佐郎庾自直等撰《長洲玉鏡》等書十餘部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Secretariat Scholar and received orders, together with Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shinan, Editing Assistant Yu Zizhi, and others, to compile more than ten works including the Longzhou Jade Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Secretariat Scholar and received orders, together with Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shinan, Editing Assistant Yu Zizhi, and others, to compile more than ten works including the Longzhou Jade Mirror.

sentences.zh: 綽所筆削，帝未嘗不稱善，而官竟不遷。

translations.literal: Whatever Chuo edited, the emperor never failed to praise — yet his office was never promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Chuo edited, the emperor never failed to praise — yet his office was never promoted.

sentences.zh: 初為校書郎，以籓邸左右，加宣惠尉。

translations.literal: Initially he served as Collator; because he was close to the princely residence, he was additionally made Captain of Manifest Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he served as Collator; because he was close to the princely residence, he was additionally made Captain of Manifest Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 遷著作佐郎，與虞世南、庾自直、蔡允恭等四人常居禁中，以文翰待詔，恩盼隆洽。
