translations.literal: Transferred to Editing Assistant, he and Yu Shinan, Yu Zizhi, Cai Yungong, and three others constantly resided within the palace precincts, awaiting edicts as literary scribes — imperial favor warm and generous.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Editing Assistant, he and Yu Shinan, Yu Zizhi, Cai Yungong, and three others constantly resided within the palace precincts, awaiting edicts as literary scribes — imperial favor was warm and generous.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，帝舍臨海頓，見大鳥，異之，詔綽為銘。

translations.literal: On the eastern campaign against Liaodong, when the emperor stopped at Linhai Station he saw a great bird and found it wondrous; he ordered Chuo to compose an inscription.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign against Liaodong, when the emperor stopped at Linhai Station he saw a great bird and found it wondrous; he ordered Chuo to compose an inscription.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The inscription reads:
translations.idiomatic: The inscription reads:

sentences.zh: 維大業八年，歲在壬申，夏四月丙子，皇帝底定遼碣，班師振旅，龍駕南轅，鸞旗西邁，行宮次於柳城縣之臨海頓焉。

translations.literal: In the great eighth year of Daye, the year being renshen, on bingzi day of the fourth month of summer — the emperor having settled Liaodong and its rocky shores, withdrawing the army in triumph, the dragon carriage turning its shafts south, the empress banner proceeding west — the traveling palace halted at Linhai Station in Liucheng county.
translations.idiomatic: In the great eighth year of Daye, the year being renshen, on bingzi day of the fourth month of summer — the emperor having settled Liaodong and its rocky shores, withdrawing the army in triumph, the dragon carriage turning south, the empress banner proceeding west — the traveling palace halted at Linhai Station in Liucheng county.

sentences.zh: 山川明秀，實仙都也。

translations.literal: The mountains and rivers were bright and beautiful — truly an immortal capital.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains and rivers were bright and beautiful — truly an immortal capital.

sentences.zh: 旌門外設，款跨重阜，帳殿周施，降望大壑。

translations.literal: The banner gate was set outside; pavilions boldly spanned the layered heights; tent palaces spread all around, descending to view the great ravine.
translations.idiomatic: The banner gate was set outside; pavilions boldly spanned the layered heights; tent palaces spread all around, descending to view the great ravine.

sentences.zh: 息清蹕，下輕輿，警百靈，綏萬福，踐素砂，步碧沚。

translations.literal: He rested the clearing guard, descended from the light carriage, alerted the hundred spirits, soothed the myriad blessings, trod white sand, and walked upon green islets.
translations.idiomatic: He rested the clearing guard, descended from the light carriage, alerted the hundred spirits, soothed the myriad blessings, trod white sand, and walked upon green islets.

sentences.zh: 同軒皇之襄野，邁漢宗於河上，想汾射以開襟，望蓬瀛而載佇。

translations.literal: Like Xuanyuan on the fields of Xiang; surpassing the Han emperor on the river — thinking of Fen and She to open the breast, gazing toward Penglai and Yingzhou and pausing long.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Yellow Emperor on the fields of Xiang, surpassing the Han emperor on the river — thinking of Fen and She to open the breast, gazing toward Penglai and Yingzhou and pausing long.

sentences.zh: 窅然齊肅，藐屬殊庭，兼以聖德遐宣，息別風與淮雨，休符潛感，表重潤於夷波。

translations.literal: Distantly all was solemn order, faintly belonging to a separate realm — moreover the sage virtue spread afar, calming the wind of Bie and rain of Huai; auspicious tokens subtly stirred, showing deep moisture on the foreign waves.
translations.idiomatic: Distantly all was solemn order, faintly belonging to a separate realm — moreover sage virtue spread afar, calming the winds of Bie and the rains of Huai; auspicious tokens subtly stirred, showing deep moisture on the foreign waves.

sentences.zh: 璧日曬光，卿雲舒采，六合開朗，十洲澄鏡。

translations.literal: The jade sun spread its light; ministerial clouds unfurled their colors; the six directions opened clear; the ten isles became a polished mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The jade sun spread its light; ministerial clouds unfurled their colors; the six directions opened clear; the ten isles became a polished mirror.

sentences.zh: 少選之間，倏焉靈感，忽有祥禽，皎同鶴鷺，出自霄漢，翻然雙下。

translations.literal: Within a brief interval, suddenly came spiritual response — suddenly an auspicious bird, bright as crane and egret, emerged from the Milky Way and gracefully descended in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Within a brief interval, suddenly came spiritual response — an auspicious bird, bright as crane and egret, emerged from the Milky Way and gracefully descended in pairs.

sentences.zh: 高逾一丈，長乃盈尋，靡霜暉於羽翮，激丹華於觜距。

translations.literal: Its height exceeded one zhang; its length filled a xun; frost-brightness spread across its wings and pinions; crimson brilliance flashed at beak and talons.
translations.idiomatic: Its height exceeded one zhang; its length filled a xun; frost-brightness spread across its wings and pinions; crimson brilliance flashed at beak and talons.

sentences.zh: 鸞翔鳳跱，鵲起鴻騫，或蹶或啄，載飛載止，徘徊馴擾，咫尺乘輿。

translations.literal: Like phoenix soaring and feng perched, magpie rising and swan ascending — now pecking, now probing, now flying, now resting; circling tame and docile, within inches of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Like phoenix soaring and feng perched, magpie rising and swan ascending — now pecking, now probing, now flying, now resting; circling tame and docile, within inches of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 不藉揮琴，非因拊石，樂我君德，是用來儀。

translations.literal: Not relying on plucked zither, not through struck stone — delighting in our lord's virtue, therefore coming as an auspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: Not relying on plucked zither, not through struck stone — delighting in our lord's virtue, therefore coming as an auspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 斯固類仙人之騏驥，冠羽族之宗長，西王青鳥，東海赤雁，豈可同年而語哉！

translations.literal: This truly resembles the immortal's fine steed, crowning the feathered kind as their chieftain — Queen Mother of the West's blue bird, East Sea's red wild goose — how could they be spoken of in the same breath!
translations.idiomatic: This truly resembles the immortal's fine steed, crowning the feathered kind as their chieftain — Queen Mother of the West's blue bird, East Sea's red wild goose — how could they be spoken of in the same breath!

sentences.zh: 竊以銘基華嶽，事乖靈異，紀跡鄒山，義非盡美，猶方冊不泯，遺文可觀。

translations.literal: I venture to say that inscribing the foundation on Mount Hua — the matter diverges from the spiritual and strange; recording traces on Mount Zou — the meaning is not wholly perfect — yet still the official records are not extinguished and the surviving text can be viewed.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to say that inscribing the foundation on Mount Hua — the matter diverges from the spiritual and strange; recording traces on Mount Zou — the meaning is not wholly perfect — yet still the official records are not extinguished and the surviving text can be viewed.

sentences.zh: 況盛德成功，若斯懿鑠，懷真味道，加此感通，不鐫名山，安用銘異！

translations.literal: How much more when success accompanies flourishing virtue, radiant as this, embracing truth and savoring the Way, with such spiritual communion added — if not carved on a famous mountain, what need for an inscription of wonder!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when success accompanies flourishing virtue, radiant as this, embracing truth and savoring the Way, with such spiritual communion added — if not carved on a famous mountain, what need for an inscription of wonder!

sentences.zh: 臣拜稽首，敢勒銘云：

translations.literal: I, your minister, bow and knock my head; I venture to inscribe the memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: I, your minister, bow and knock my head; I venture to inscribe the memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 來蘇興怨，帝自東征，言複禹績，乃禦軒營。

translations.literal: When the people returned to life, grievance rose — the emperor himself marched east, saying he would restore Yu's achievements, and then mounted his camp carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the people returned to life, grievance rose — the emperor himself marched east, saying he would restore Yu's achievements, and then mounted his camp carriage.

sentences.zh: 六師薄伐，三韓肅清，龔行天罰，赫赫明明。

translations.literal: The six armies pressed close in punitive strike; the three Han were swept clear; he marched bearing Heaven's punishment — resplendent and bright.
translations.idiomatic: The six armies pressed close in punitive strike; the three Han were swept clear; he marched bearing Heaven's punishment — resplendent and bright.

sentences.zh: 文德上暢，靈武外薄，車徒不擾，苛慝靡作。

translations.literal: Civil virtue flowed aloft; martial spirit spread outward; chariots and foot soldiery were undisturbed; harsh evil did not arise.
translations.idiomatic: Civil virtue flowed aloft; martial spirit spread outward; chariots and foot soldiery were undisturbed; harsh evil did not arise.

sentences.zh: 凱歌載路，成功允鑠，反旆還軒，遵林並壑。

translations.literal: Victory songs filled the roads; success was true and brilliant; turning banners, returning the carriage, following forests and ravines together.
translations.idiomatic: Victory songs filled the roads; success was true and brilliant; turning banners, returning the carriage, following forests and ravines together.

sentences.zh: 停輿海澨，駐驛岩阯，窅想遐凝，藐屬千里。

translations.literal: Halt the carriage at the sea's edge; rest the relay station at the rocky shore — distant thoughts gathered in contemplation, faintly spanning a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Halt the carriage at the sea's edge; rest the relay station at the rocky shore — distant thoughts gathered in contemplation, faintly spanning a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 金台銀闕，雲浮嶽峙，有感斯應，靈禽效祉。

translations.literal: Golden terraces and silver towers — clouds floating, peaks standing; where feeling stirs, response comes; the spirit bird manifests blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Golden terraces and silver towers — clouds floating, peaks standing; where feeling stirs, response comes; the spirit bird manifests blessing.

sentences.zh: 飛來清漢，俱集華泉，好音玉響，皓質水鮮。

translations.literal: Flying in from the clear Milky Way, all gathering at the glorious spring — fine sounds like jade ringing, white substance fresh as water.
translations.idiomatic: Flying in from the clear Milky Way, all gathering at the glorious spring — fine sounds like jade ringing, white substance fresh as water.

sentences.zh: 狎仁馴德，習習翩翩，絕跡無泯，于萬斯年。

translations.literal: Growing intimate with benevolence, tame in virtue — gently, gracefully — its departing traces never extinguished, for ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Growing intimate with benevolence, tame in virtue — gently, gracefully — its departing traces never extinguished, for ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，命有司勒於海上。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved, ordering the relevant offices to inscribe it on the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and approved, ordering the relevant offices to inscribe it on the seashore.

sentences.zh: 以渡遼功，授建節尉。

translations.literal: For merit in crossing to Liaodong, he was appointed Commandant Bearing the Staff.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in crossing to Liaodong, he was appointed Commandant Bearing the Staff.

sentences.zh: 綽恃才任氣，無所降下。

translations.literal: Chuo relied on his talent and indulged his temperament, deferring to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo relied on his talent and indulged his temperament, deferring to no one.

sentences.zh: 著作郎諸葛潁以學業幸於帝，綽每輕侮之，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Editing Clerk Zhuge Ying, favored by the emperor for his scholarship, was constantly slighted by Chuo — hence enmity arose.
translations.idiomatic: Editing Clerk Zhuge Ying, favored by the emperor for his scholarship, was constantly slighted by Chuo — hence enmity arose.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問綽於潁，潁曰：「虞綽粗人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Ying about Chuo; Ying said: "Yu Chuo is a coarse man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Ying about Chuo; Ying said: "Yu Chuo is a coarse man.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded assent.

sentences.zh: 時禮部尚書楊玄感稱為貴倨，虛襟禮之，與結布衣之友。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan was said to be proud and aloof; Chuo opened his bosom and treated him with courtesy, forming a friendship of plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan was said to be proud and aloof; Chuo opened his bosom and treated him with courtesy, forming a friendship of plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 綽數從之遊。

translations.literal: Chuo often accompanied him in his outings.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo often accompanied him in his outings.

sentences.zh: 其族人虞世南誡之曰：「上性猜忌，而君過厚玄感。

translations.literal: His clansman Yu Shinan admonished him: "The emperor's nature is suspicious, yet you treat Xuangan with excessive warmth.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Yu Shinan admonished him: "The emperor's nature is suspicious, yet you treat Xuangan with excessive warmth.

sentences.zh: 若與絕交者，帝知君改悔，可以無咎；

translations.literal: If you break off the friendship, when the emperor knows you have repented, you may escape blame;
translations.idiomatic: If you break off the friendship, when the emperor knows you have repented, you may escape blame;

sentences.zh: 不然，終當見禍。」

translations.literal: otherwise, in the end you will surely meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, in the end you will surely meet disaster.

sentences.zh: 綽不從。

translations.literal: Chuo did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 尋有告綽以禁內兵書借玄感，帝甚銜之。

translations.literal: Before long someone reported that Chuo had lent Xuangan military books from within the palace precincts; the emperor deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone reported that Chuo had lent Xuangan military books from within the palace precincts; the emperor deeply harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗後，籍沒其家，妓妾併入宮。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, his household was confiscated and his courtesans and concubines were all taken into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, his household was confiscated and his courtesans and concubines were all taken into the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝因問之，玄感平常時與何人交往，其妾以虞綽對。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon asked whom Xuangan ordinarily associated with; one of his concubines named Yu Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon asked whom Xuangan ordinarily associated with; one of his concubines named Yu Chuo.

sentences.zh: 帝令大理卿鄭善果窮治其事，綽曰：「羈旅薄游，與玄感文酒談款，實無他謀。」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Chief Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo to investigate thoroughly; Chuo said: "As a traveler wandering far, I exchanged literary conversation and wine with Xuangan — truly no other design.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Chief Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo to investigate thoroughly; Chuo said: "As a traveler wandering far, I exchanged literary conversation and wine with Xuangan — truly no other design.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不解，徙綽且末。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger was not appeased, and Chuo was exiled to Qiemao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's anger was not appeased, and Chuo was exiled to Qiemao.

sentences.zh: 綽至長安而亡，吏逮之急，於是潛渡江，變姓名，自稱吳卓。

translations.literal: Chuo reached Chang'an and fled; officials pressed the pursuit urgently — whereupon he secretly crossed the river, changed his name, and called himself Wu Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo reached Chang'an and fled; officials pressed the pursuit urgently — whereupon he secretly crossed the river, changed his name, and called himself Wu Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 游東陽，抵信安令天水辛大德，大德舍之。

translations.literal: Roaming to Dongyang, he came to Xin Dade, Magistrate of Xin'an in Tianshui; Dade gave him lodging.
translations.idiomatic: Roaming to Dongyang, he came to Xin Dade, Magistrate of Xin'an in Tianshui; Dade gave him lodging.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，綽與人爭田相訟，因有識綽者而告之，竟為吏所執，坐斬江都，時年五十四。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Chuo had a land dispute with someone and went to court; because someone recognized Chuo and reported him, he was finally seized by officials and executed at Jiangdu, at age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, Chuo had a land dispute with someone and went to court; because someone recognized him and reported him, he was finally seized by officials and executed at Jiangdu at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 所有詞賦，並行於世。

translations.literal: All his poetry and rhapsodies circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: All his poetry and rhapsodies circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 大德為令，誅翦群盜，甚得民和。

translations.literal: Dade as magistrate exterminated bandit gangs and greatly won the people's accord.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate, Dade exterminated bandit gangs and greatly won the people's accord.

sentences.zh: 與綽俱為使者所執，其妻泣曰：「每諫君無匿學士，今日之事，豈不哀哉！」

translations.literal: He and Chuo were both seized by the messenger; his wife wept and said: "I repeatedly admonished you not to harbor scholars — today's affair — is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: He and Chuo were both seized by the messenger; his wife wept and said: "I repeatedly admonished you not to harbor scholars — today's affair — is it not pitiful!

sentences.zh: 大德笑曰：「我本圖脫長者，反為人告之，吾罪也。

translations.literal: Dade smiled and said: "I originally intended to help a worthy man escape — instead I was reported by someone; this is my fault.
translations.idiomatic: Dade smiled and said: "I originally intended to help a worthy man escape — instead I was reported by someone; this is my fault.

sentences.zh: 當死以謝綽。」

translations.literal: I should die to answer to Chuo."
translations.idiomatic: I should die to answer to Chuo."

sentences.zh: 會有詔，死罪得以擊賊自效。

translations.literal: Just then there was an edict that those guilty of capital crimes might redeem themselves by striking bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Just then there was an edict that those guilty of capital crimes might redeem themselves by striking bandits.

sentences.zh: 信安吏民詣使者叩頭曰：「辛君人命所懸，辛君若去，亦無信安矣。」

translations.literal: The officials and people of Xin'an came to the messenger and knocked their heads, saying: "Magistrate Xin's life is what hangs in the balance — if Magistrate Xin departs, there will be no Xin'an left.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Xin'an came to the messenger and kowtowed, saying: "Magistrate Xin's life is what hangs in the balance — if Magistrate Xin departs, there will be no Xin'an left.

sentences.zh: 使者留之以討賊。

translations.literal: The messenger kept him to suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger kept him to suppress bandits.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，斬使者，大德獲全。

translations.literal: The emperor raged and executed the messenger; Dade was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged and executed the messenger; Dade was spared.

sentences.zh: 王胄，字承基，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, courtesy name Shengji, was a native of Linyi in Langya commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou, courtesy name Shengji, was a native of Linyi in Langya commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖筠，梁太子詹事。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun served as Steward of the Heir Apparent under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun served as Steward of the Heir Apparent under the Liang dynasty.

sentences.zh: 父祥，陳黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Xiang served as Attendant at the Yellow Gate under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang served as Attendant at the Yellow Gate under Chen.

sentences.zh: 胄少有逸才，仕陳，起家鄱陽王法曹參軍，曆太子舍人、東陽王文學。

translations.literal: Zhou from youth had exceptional talent; serving Chen, he began his career as Legal Officer Aide to the Prince of Poyang and served successively as Attendant of the Crown Prince and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou from youth had exceptional talent; serving Chen, he began his career as Legal Officer Aide to the Prince of Poyang and served successively as Attendant of the Crown Prince and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，晉王廣引為學士。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Prince of Jin Yang Guang brought him in as Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Prince of Jin Yang Guang brought him in as Literary Scholar.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，從劉方擊林邑，以功授帥都督。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou he followed Liu Fang in attacking Linyi and for merit was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Renshou era he served under Liu Fang in the attack on Linyi and for merit was appointed Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為著作佐郎，以文詞為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he served as Editing Assistant; his literary compositions were highly valued by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he served as Editing Assistant; his literary compositions were highly valued by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 帝常自東都還京師，賜天下大酺，因為五言詩，詔胄和之。

translations.literal: The emperor often returned from the Eastern Capital to the capital, granting a grand feast throughout the realm; he thereupon composed a pentasyllabic poem and ordered Zhou to harmonize with it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often returned from the Eastern Capital to the capital, granting a grand feast throughout the realm; he thereupon composed a pentasyllabic poem and ordered Zhou to harmonize with it.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：「河洛稱朝市，崤函實奧區。

translations.literal: The lyrics read: "The Yellow and Luo are called the court's marketplace; Xiao and Han are truly the heartland.
translations.idiomatic: The lyrics read: "The Yellow and Luo are called the court's marketplace; Xiao and Han are truly the heartland.

sentences.zh: 周營曲阜作，漢建奉春謨。

translations.literal: Zhou established its rule at Qufu; Han founded its capital on Fengchun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou established its rule at Qufu; Han founded its capital on Fengchun's counsel.

sentences.zh: 大君苞二代，皇居盛兩都。

translations.literal: The great lord embraces two dynasties; the imperial dwelling flourishes in two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: Our great lord embraces two dynasties; his imperial seat flourishes in twin capitals.

sentences.zh: 招搖正東指，天駟乃西驅。

translations.literal: The Dipper points true east; the Heavenly Team now drives west.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper points due east; the Heavenly Team now drives westward.

sentences.zh: 展軨齊玉軑，式道耀金吾。

translations.literal: Extending axles, jade hubs aligned; clearing the road, the Golden Guard gleams.
translations.idiomatic: Axles unfold with jade hubs aligned; the route-clearing guard gleams in gold.

sentences.zh: 千門駐罕罼，四達儼車徒。

translations.literal: At a thousand gates the imperial hunt-net halts; on four thoroughfares chariots and foot soldiers stand in order.
translations.idiomatic: At a thousand gates the imperial hunt-net halts; on four thoroughfares chariots and foot soldiers stand in ordered ranks.

sentences.zh: 是節春之暮，神皋華實敷。

translations.literal: This season is spring's end; the sacred fields spread flowers and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: This season marks the end of spring; the sacred fields spread flowers and fruit in abundance.

sentences.zh: 皇情感時物，睿思屬枌榆。

translations.literal: The emperor's feelings respond to seasonal things; his sage thoughts turn to elm and scholar-tree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart responds to the season; his sage thoughts turn homeward.

sentences.zh: 詔問百年老，恩隆五日酺。

translations.literal: An edict inquires after centenarians; grace magnifies the five-day feast.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts inquire after centenarians; imperial grace magnifies the five day feast.

sentences.zh: 小人荷熔鑄，何由答大爐。」

translations.literal: I, the lesser man, bear smelting and casting — how can I answer the great furnace?
translations.idiomatic: I, the lesser man, have received smelting and casting — how can I answer the great furnace?

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，因謂侍臣曰：「氣高致遠，歸之於胄；

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved, then said to his attendants: "Lofty spirit reaching far — this belongs to Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and approved, then said to his attendants: "Lofty spirit reaching far — that belongs to Zhou;

sentences.zh: 詞清體潤，其在世基；

translations.literal: clear words and polished style belong to Shiji;
translations.idiomatic: clear words and polished style belong to Shiji;

sentences.zh: 意密理新，推庾自直。

translations.literal: dense meaning and fresh reasoning — I put forward Yu Zizhi.
translations.idiomatic: dense meaning and fresh reasoning — I put forward Yu Zizhi.

sentences.zh: 過此者，未可以言詩也。」

translations.literal: Beyond these, one cannot speak of poetry."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these, one cannot speak of poetry at all."

sentences.zh: 帝所有篇什，多令繼和。

translations.literal: Of all the emperor's compositions, he often ordered Zhou to harmonize with them.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the emperor's compositions, he often ordered Zhou to harmonize with them.

sentences.zh: 與虞綽齊名，同志友善，于時後進之士咸以二人為准的。

translations.literal: Famous alongside Yu Chuo, kindred in spirit and friendly; at the time aspiring scholars all took the two as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Famous alongside Yu Chuo, kindred in spirit and friendly, at the time aspiring scholars all took the two as their standard.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，進授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 胄性疏率不倫，自恃才大，鬱鬱于薄宦，每負氣陵傲，忽略時人。

translations.literal: Zhou's nature was loose and unconventional; relying on his great talent, he brooded over low offices, often arrogant and overbearing, disdaining contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's nature was loose and unconventional; relying on his great talent, he brooded over low offices, often arrogant and overbearing, and disdained his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 為諸葛潁所嫉，屢譖之於帝，帝愛其才而不罪。

translations.literal: Envied by Zhuge Ying, who repeatedly slandered him to the emperor; the emperor loved his talent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Envied by Zhuge Ying, who repeatedly slandered him to the emperor, the emperor loved his talent and did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感虛襟與交，數遊其第。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan, with open mind, befriended him and often visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan, with an open mind, befriended him and often visited his residence.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，與虞綽俱徙邊。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, he and Yu Chuo were both exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, he and Yu Chuo were both exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 胄遂亡匿，潛還江左，為吏所捕，坐誅，時年五十六。

translations.literal: Zhou then fled into hiding, secretly returned to Jiangzuo, was captured by officials, and executed at age fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou then fled into hiding and secretly returned to Jiangzuo; captured by officials, he was executed at the age of fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 所著詞賦，多行於世。

translations.literal: His poetry and rhapsodies widely circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and rhapsodies widely circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 胄兄眘，字元恭，博學多通。

translations.literal: Zhou's elder brother Shen, courtesy name Yuangong, was broadly learned and thoroughly versed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's elder brother Shen, courtesy name Yuangong, was broadly learned and thoroughly versed.

sentences.zh: 少有盛名于江左。

translations.literal: From youth he enjoyed great fame in Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he enjoyed great fame in Jiangzuo.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，曆太子洗馬、中舍人。

translations.literal: Serving Chen, he successively held the posts of Attendant Cavalry for the Crown Prince and Central Household Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Chen, he successively held the posts of Attendant Cavalry for the Crown Prince and Central Household Attendant.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，與胄俱為學士。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he and Zhou both became Literary Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he and Zhou both became Literary Scholars.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，授秘書郎，卒官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman and died in office.

sentences.zh: 庾自直，潁川人也。

translations.literal: Yu Zizhi was a native of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zizhi was a native of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父持，陳羽林監。

translations.literal: His father Chi served as Forest Guard Supervisor under Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi served as Forest Guard Supervisor under Chen.

sentences.zh: 自直少好學，沉靜寡欲。

translations.literal: Zizhi from youth loved learning; he was calm, reserved, and had few desires.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zizhi loved learning; he was calm, reserved, and had few desires.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，曆豫章王府外兵參軍、宣惠記室。

translations.literal: Serving Chen, he successively held the posts of External Military Aide to the Prince of Yuzhang and Recorder of Manifest Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Chen, he successively held the posts of External Military Aide to the Prince of Yuzhang and Recorder of Manifest Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 陳亡，入關，不得調。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, he entered the passes but could not obtain appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, he entered the passes but could not obtain appointment.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣聞之，引為學士。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Yang Guang heard of him and brought him in as Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Yang Guang heard of him and brought him in as Literary Scholar.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Editing Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Editing Assistant.

sentences.zh: 自直解屬文，于五言詩尤善。

translations.literal: Zizhi was versed in literary composition and especially skilled at pentasyllabic poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi was versed in literary composition and especially skilled at pentasyllabic poetry.

sentences.zh: 性恭慎，不妄交遊，特為帝所愛。

translations.literal: His nature was respectful and cautious; he did not socialize lightly and was especially favored by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and cautious by nature, he did not socialize lightly and was especially favored by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝有篇章，必先示自直，令其詆訶。

translations.literal: When the emperor had compositions, he always first showed them to Zizhi and ordered him to criticize them.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had compositions, he always first showed them to Zizhi and ordered him to criticize them.

sentences.zh: 自直所難，帝輒改之，或至於再三，俟其稱善，然後方出。

translations.literal: Whatever Zizhi faulted, the emperor at once revised, sometimes two or three times, waiting until he praised it before releasing it.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Zizhi faulted, the emperor at once revised, sometimes two or three times, waiting until he praised it before releasing it.

sentences.zh: 其見親禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intimacy and honor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the intimacy and honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 後以本官知起居舍人事。

translations.literal: Later, while retaining his original rank, he oversaw the duties of Court Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while retaining his original rank, he oversaw the duties of Court Diarist.

sentences.zh: 化及作逆，以之北上，自載露車中，感激發病卒。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled, he was taken north; riding in an open cart, he was stirred to illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji rebelled, he was taken north; riding in an open cart, he was stirred to illness and died.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: A collected works in ten fascicles circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collected works in ten fascicles circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 潘徽，字伯彥，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Pan Hui, courtesy name Boyan, was a native of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hui, courtesy name Boyan, was a native of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，少受《禮》于鄭灼，受《毛詩》于施公，受《書》于張沖，講《莊》、《老》于張譏，並通大義。

translations.literal: Intelligent by nature, in youth he studied the Rites under Zheng Zhuo, the Mao Odes under Master Shi, the Documents under Zhang Chong, and the Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhang Ji — mastering the great principles of all.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent by nature, in youth he studied the Rites under Zheng Zhuo, the Mao Odes under Master Shi, the Documents under Zhang Chong, and the Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhang Ji, mastering the great principles of all.

sentences.zh: 尤精三史。

translations.literal: He was especially proficient in the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially proficient in the Three Histories.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，能持論。

translations.literal: He was skilled at literary composition and capable in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and capable in debate.

sentences.zh: 陳尚書令江總引致文儒之士，徽一詣總，總甚敬之。

translations.literal: Jiang Zong, Minister of Works of Chen, gathered literary scholars; Hui paid him one visit and Jiang greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong, Minister of Works of Chen, gathered literary scholars; Hui paid him one visit and Jiang greatly respected him.

sentences.zh: 釋褐新蔡王國侍郎，選為客館令。

translations.literal: Upon first appointment he served as Gentleman of the Prince of Xincai's domain and was selected as Keeper of the Guest Hostel.
translations.idiomatic: Upon first appointment he served as Gentleman of the Prince of Xincai's domain and was selected as Keeper of the Guest Hostel.

sentences.zh: 隋遣魏澹聘于陳，陳人使徽接對之。

translations.literal: Sui sent Wei Dan as envoy to Chen; the Chen court had Hui receive and respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sent Wei Dan as envoy to Chen; the Chen court had Hui receive and respond to him.

sentences.zh: 澹將返命，為啟于陳主曰：「敬奉弘慈，曲垂餞送。」

translations.literal: Dan was about to return with his report and wrote a memorial to the Chen ruler, saying: "Respectfully receiving your vast kindness, you graciously saw us off.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was about to return with his report and wrote a memorial to the Chen ruler, saying: "Respectfully receiving your vast kindness, you graciously saw us off.

sentences.zh: 徽以為「伏奉」為重，「敬奉」為輕，卻其啟而不奏。

translations.literal: Hui held that "prostrate submission" was weighty while "respectful submission" was light; he rejected the memorial and did not submit it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui held that "prostrate submission" was weighty while "respectful submission" was light; he rejected the memorial and did not submit it.

sentences.zh: 澹立議曰：「《曲禮》注曰：『禮主於敬。』

translations.literal: Dan set forth his argument, saying: "The commentary on the Qu Li says: 'Rites are rooted in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Dan set forth his argument, saying: "The commentary on the Qu Li says: 'Rites are rooted in reverence.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：『維桑與梓，必恭敬止。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Of mulberry and catalpa, one must be reverent and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 'Of mulberry and catalpa, one must be reverent and respectful.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》曰：『宗廟致高。』

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'In the ancestral temple, reverence reaches its height.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'In the ancestral temple, reverence reaches its height.

sentences.zh: 又云：『不敬其親，謂之悖禮。』

translations.literal: It also says: 'Not revering one's parents is called violating the rites.
translations.idiomatic: It also says: 'Not revering one's parents is called violating the rites.

sentences.zh: 孔子敬天之怒，成湯聖敬日躋。

translations.literal: Confucius revered Heaven's wrath; King Cheng of Tang daily ascended in sage reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius revered Heaven's wrath; King Cheng of Tang daily ascended in sage reverence.

sentences.zh: 宗廟極重，上天極高，父極尊，君極貴，四者咸同一敬，五經未有異文，不知以敬為輕，竟何所據？」

translations.literal: The ancestral temple is supremely weighty, Heaven supremely high, the father supremely honored, the ruler supremely exalted — all four share the same reverence; the Five Classics nowhere give divergent readings — on what ground do you hold reverence to be light?'
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple is supremely weighty, Heaven supremely high, the father supremely honored, the ruler supremely exalted — all four share the same reverence; the Five Classics nowhere give divergent readings — on what ground do you hold reverence to be light?'

sentences.zh: 徽難之曰：「向所論敬字，本不全以為輕，但施用處殊，義成通別。

translations.literal: Hui challenged him, saying: "In what I argued earlier about the word 'reverence,' I did not wholly treat it as light — only its application differs from place to place, so the meaning becomes general in one case and particular in another.
translations.idiomatic: Hui challenged him, saying: "In what I argued earlier about the word 'reverence,' I did not wholly treat it as light — only its application differs from place to place, so the meaning becomes general in one case and particular in another.

sentences.zh: 《禮》主於敬，此是通言，猶如男子『冠而字之』，注云『成人敬其名也』。

translations.literal: That rites are rooted in reverence is a general statement — just as when a man 'is capped and given a style name,' the commentary says 'as an adult he is reverent toward his personal name.'"
translations.idiomatic: That rites are rooted in reverence is a general statement — just as when a man 'is capped and given a style name,' the commentary says 'as an adult he is reverent toward his personal name.'"

sentences.zh: 《春秋》有冀缺，夫妻亦云『相敬』。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn Annals there is Ji Que; husband and wife are also said to 'show mutual reverence.'"
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn Annals there is Ji Que; husband and wife are also said to 'show mutual reverence.'"

sentences.zh: 既於子則有敬名之義，在夫亦有敬妻之說，此可複並謂極重乎？

translations.literal: If toward a son there is the meaning of reverence for the personal name, and toward a husband there is also talk of revering the wife — can these likewise all be called supremely weighty?
translations.idiomatic: If toward a son there is the meaning of reverence for the personal name, and toward a husband there is also talk of revering the wife — can these likewise all be called supremely weighty?

sentences.zh: 至若『敬謝諸公』，固非尊地，『公子敬愛'，止施賓友，『敬問』『敬報』，彌見雷同，『敬聽』『敬酬』，何關貴隔！

translations.literal: As for 'respectfully thanking the lords,' that is plainly not a place of supreme honor; 'the prince respectfully loves' applies only to guests and friends; 'respectful inquiry' and 'respectful reply' show all the more how formulaic it is; 'respectful listening' and 'respectful response' — what have they to do with rank and distance!
translations.idiomatic: As for 'respectfully thanking the lords,' that is plainly not a place of supreme honor; 'the prince respectfully loves' applies only to guests and friends; 'respectful inquiry' and 'respectful reply' show all the more how formulaic it is; 'respectful listening' and 'respectful response' — what have they to do with rank and distance!

sentences.zh: 當知敬之為義，雖是不輕，但敬之於語，則有時混漫。

translations.literal: One should know that as a principle reverence is not light — yet in language, reverence sometimes becomes vague and indiscriminate.
translations.idiomatic: One should know that as a principle reverence is not light — yet in language, reverence sometimes becomes vague and indiscriminate.

sentences.zh: 今云『敬奉』，所以成疑。

translations.literal: To say 'respectful submission' here is what gives rise to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: To say 'respectful submission' here is what gives rise to doubt.

sentences.zh: 聊舉一隅，未為深據。」

translations.literal: I have merely offered one corner of the matter — this is not yet deep proof."
translations.idiomatic: I have merely offered one corner of the matter — this is not yet deep proof."

sentences.zh: 澹不能對，遂從而改焉。

translations.literal: Dan could not reply and thereupon changed his wording accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Dan could not reply and thereupon changed his wording accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，為州博士，秦孝王俊聞其名，召為學士。

translations.literal: When Chen fell he served as prefectural doctor; Prince Jun of Qin Xiaowang heard his name and summoned him as Literary Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he served as prefectural doctor; Prince Jun of Qin Xiaowang heard his name and summoned him as Literary Scholar.

sentences.zh: 嘗從俊朝京師，在途，令徽於馬上為賦，行一驛而成，名曰《述恩賦》。

translations.literal: Once, accompanying Jun to the capital, on the road he ordered Hui to compose a rhapsody on horseback; finished in the distance of one post station, it was titled Rhapsody on Expressing Gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying Jun to the capital, on the road he ordered Hui to compose a rhapsody on horseback; finished within one post station's travel, it was titled Rhapsody on Expressing Gratitude.

sentences.zh: 俊覽而善之。

translations.literal: Jun read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jun read it and approved.

sentences.zh: 複令為《萬字文》，並遣撰集字書，名為《韻篡》。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Ten Thousand Character Essay and commissioned compilation of a character book named Rhyme Compendium.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the Ten Thousand Character Essay and commissioned compilation of a character book named Rhyme Compendium.

sentences.zh: 徽為序曰：

translations.literal: Hui composed a preface, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hui composed a preface, saying:

sentences.zh: 文字之來尚矣。

translations.literal: The origin of writing is very ancient.
translations.idiomatic: The origin of writing is very ancient.

sentences.zh: 初則羲皇出震，觀象緯以法天，次則史頡佐軒，察蹄跡而取地。

translations.literal: At first Fuxi emerged with the thunder, observing celestial patterns to model Heaven; next Cang Jie assisted Xuanyuan, examining hoofprints to take the measure of earth.
translations.idiomatic: At first Fuxi emerged with the thunder, observing celestial patterns to model Heaven; next Cang Jie assisted the Yellow Emperor, examining hoofprints to take the measure of earth.

sentences.zh: 於是八卦爰始，爻文斯作，繩用既息，墳籍生焉。

translations.literal: Then the Eight Trigrams began, line-and-script arose, knotted cords ceased to serve, and written records were born.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Eight Trigrams began, line-and-script arose, knotted cords ceased to serve, and written records were born.

sentences.zh: 至如龍策授河，龜威出洛，綠綈白檢，述勳、華之運，金繩玉字，表殷、夏之符，銜甲示于姬壇，吐卷徵于孔室，莫不理包遠邇，跡會幽明，仰協神功，俯照人事。

translations.literal: Consider the dragon tally given at the river, the tortoise omen emerging from the Luo; green silk and white tablets recording the fortunes of Emperor Xun and Emperor Hua; gold cords and jade characters marking the tokens of Yin and Xia; armor-bearing shells shown at the Ji altar, scrolls disgorged as signs at Confucius's house — all embraced near and far in principle, traces meeting in dark and light, above harmonizing with divine power, below illuminating human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the dragon tally given at the river, the tortoise omen emerging from the Luo; green silk and white tablets recording the fortunes of Emperor Xun and Emperor Hua; gold cords and jade characters marking the tokens of Yin and Xia; armor-bearing shells shown at the Ji altar, scrolls disgorged as signs at Confucius's house — all embraced near and far in principle, traces meeting in dark and light, above harmonizing with divine power, below illuminating human affairs.

sentences.zh: 其製作也如彼，其祥瑞也如此，故能宣流萬代，正名百物，為生民之耳目，作後王之模範，頌美形容，垂芬篆素。

translations.literal: Its creation was thus, its auspicious signs like this — therefore it could spread through ten thousand generations, set right the names of the hundred things, serve as the eyes and ears of the people, become the model for later kings, praise and beautify in description, and leave fragrance on bamboo slips and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Its creation was thus, its auspicious signs like this — therefore it could spread through ten thousand generations, set right the names of the hundred things, serve as the eyes and ears of the people, become the model for later kings, praise and beautify in description, and leave fragrance on bamboo slips and silk.

sentences.zh: 暨大隋之受命也，追從三五，並曜參辰，外振武功，內修文德。

translations.literal: When Great Sui received the Mandate, it followed the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, shining together with the Three Stars; outwardly it strengthened martial achievement, inwardly it cultivated civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Great Sui received the Mandate, it followed the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, shining together with the Three Stars; outwardly it strengthened martial achievement, inwardly it cultivated civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 飛英聲而勒嵩岱，彰大定而銘鐘鼎。

translations.literal: Its soaring fame was carved on Mount Song and Mount Tai; its great settlement was inscribed on bells and cauldrons.
translations.idiomatic: Its soaring fame was carved on Mount Song and Mount Tai; its great settlement was inscribed on bells and cauldrons.

sentences.zh: 春幹秋羽，盛禮樂於膠庠，省俗觀風，采歌謠于唐衛。

translations.literal: With spring plowing and autumn feathers, rites and music flourished in the schools; inspecting customs and observing local ways, ballads were gathered in Tang and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: With spring plowing and autumn feathers, rites and music flourished in the schools; inspecting customs and observing local ways, ballads were gathered in Tang and Wei.

sentences.zh: 我秦王殿下，降靈霄極，稟秀天機，質潤珪璋，文兼黼黻。

translations.literal: Our Prince of Qin, descending in spirit from the highest heaven, endowed with heaven's finest essence — his substance polished like jade and scepter-stone, his culture combining brocade and embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Our Prince of Qin, descending in spirit from the highest heaven, endowed with heaven's finest essence — his substance polished like jade and scepter-stone, his culture combining brocade and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 楚詩早習，頗屬懷於言志，沛《易》先通，每留神于索隱。

translations.literal: He early studied the poetry of Chu and greatly cherished expressing intent in words; he first mastered the expansive Changes and always kept his mind on probing hidden meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He early studied the poetry of Chu and greatly cherished expressing intent in words; he first mastered the expansive Changes and always kept his mind on probing hidden meaning.

sentences.zh: 尊儒好古，三雍之對已遒，博物多能，百家之工彌洽。

translations.literal: Revering Confucian learning and loving antiquity, his responses at the Three Yong were already forceful; broadly learned and multitalented, his mastery of the hundred schools grew ever more complete.
translations.idiomatic: Revering Confucian learning and loving antiquity, his responses at the Three Yong were already forceful; broadly learned and multitalented, his mastery of the hundred schools grew ever more complete.

sentences.zh: 遨遊必名教，漁獵唯圖史。

translations.literal: In his roaming he kept to moral teaching; in his hunting he took only charts and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In his roaming he kept to moral teaching; in his hunting he took only charts and histories.

sentences.zh: 加以降情引汲，擇善芻微，築館招賢，攀枝佇異。

translations.literal: Moreover he lowered his feelings to draw others up, chose the good even in humble fodder, built halls to summon the worthy, and waited on branches for extraordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he lowered his feelings to draw others up, chose the good even in humble fodder, built halls to summon the worthy, and waited on branches for extraordinary talent.

sentences.zh: 剖連城于井裡，賁束帛於丘園，薄技無遺，片言便賞。

translations.literal: He prized linked-city jade from village wells and honored bundles of silk in rustic gardens; no slight skill was overlooked, and a single phrase might win reward.
translations.idiomatic: He prized linked-city jade from village wells and honored bundles of silk in rustic gardens; no slight skill was overlooked, and a single phrase might win reward.

sentences.zh: 所以人加脂粉，物競琢磨，俱報稻粱，各施鳴吠。

translations.literal: Therefore people applied rouge and powder, things vied in polishing; all repaid grain and millet, each offering bark and cry.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore people applied rouge and powder, things vied in polishing; all repaid grain and millet, each offering bark and cry.

sentences.zh: 于時歲次鶉火，月躔夷則，驂駕務隙，靈光意靜。

translations.literal: At that time the year stood at Quail Fire, the moon traversed Yize; the paired chariot found leisure between duties, and spiritual light rested in quiet intent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the year stood at Quail Fire, the moon traversed Yize; the paired chariot found leisure between duties, and spiritual light rested in quiet intent.

sentences.zh: 前臨竹沼，卻倚桂岩，泉石瑩仁智之心，煙霞發文彩之致，賓僚霧集，教義風靡。

translations.literal: Facing a bamboo pond in front, leaning against cassia cliffs behind — springs and stones polished the heart of benevolence and wisdom; mist and clouds released the charm of literary color; guests and aides gathered like fog; teaching and principle spread on the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Facing a bamboo pond in front, leaning against cassia cliffs behind — springs and stones polished the heart of benevolence and wisdom; mist and clouds released the charm of literary color; guests and aides gathered like fog; teaching and principle spread on the wind.

sentences.zh: 乃討論群藝，商略眾書，以為小學之家，尤多舛雜，雖複周禮漢律，務在貫通，而巧說邪辭，遞生同異。

translations.literal: Then they discussed the various arts and weighed the many books, holding that the school of elementary learning was especially confused and mixed — though Zhou rites and Han statutes sought thorough mastery, clever arguments and perverse phrases constantly produced agreement and divergence.
translations.idiomatic: Then they discussed the various arts and weighed the many books, holding that the school of elementary learning was especially confused and mixed — though Zhou rites and Han statutes sought thorough mastery, clever arguments and perverse phrases constantly produced agreement and divergence.

sentences.zh: 且文訛篆隸，音謬楚夏，《三蒼》、《急就》之流，微存章句，《說文》、《字林》之屬，唯別體形。

translations.literal: Moreover script had erred from seal to clerical forms, pronunciation was mistaken between Chu and Xia; works like the Three Cang and Rapid Composition preserved only fragments of phrasing; works like the Shuowen and Zilin distinguished bodily forms alone.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover script had erred from seal to clerical forms, pronunciation was mistaken between Chu and Xia; works like the Three Cang and Rapid Composition preserved only fragments of phrasing; works like the Shuowen and Zilin distinguished bodily forms alone.

sentences.zh: 至於尋聲推韻，良為疑混，酌古會今，未臻功要。

translations.literal: As for tracing sound and inferring rhyme, this was truly confused and doubtful; weighing antiquity against the present, the essential achievement had not been reached.
translations.idiomatic: As for tracing sound and inferring rhyme, this was truly confused and doubtful; weighing antiquity against the present, the essential achievement had not been reached.

sentences.zh: 末有李登《聲類》、呂靜《韻集》，始判清濁，才分宮羽，而全無引據，過傷淺局，詩賦所須，卒難為用。

translations.literal: Only later did Li Deng's Sound Categories and Lu Jing's Rhyme Collection first distinguish clear and murky tones and barely divide gong and yu modes — yet they wholly lacked textual support, were overly shallow and narrow, and what poetry and rhapsody require was in the end hard to use.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did Li Deng's Sound Categories and Lu Jing's Rhyme Collection first distinguish clear and murky tones and barely divide gong and yu modes — yet they wholly lacked textual support, were overly shallow and narrow, and what poetry and rhapsody require was in the end hard to use.

sentences.zh: 遂躬紆睿旨，摽摘是非，撮舉宏綱，裁斷篇部，總會舊轍，創立新意，聲別相從，即隨注釋。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally bent to the sage command, marked out right and wrong, gathered the great outline, cut and arranged sections and parts, summed up old tracks, established new meaning — sounds distinguished and following one another, each immediately annotated.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he personally bent to the sage command, marked out right and wrong, gathered the great outline, cut and arranged sections and parts, summed up old tracks, established new meaning — sounds distinguished and following one another, each immediately annotated.

sentences.zh: 詳之詁訓，證以經史，備包《騷》《雅》，博牽子集，汗簡雲畢，題為《韻篡》，凡三十卷，勒成一家。

translations.literal: Explicating glosses in detail, verified by classics and histories, fully encompassing the Sao and Ya, broadly drawing on masters and collections — bamboo slips sweat and clouds finish; titled Rhyme Compendium, thirty fascicles in all, cut into a school of its own.
translations.idiomatic: Explicating glosses in detail, verified by classics and histories, fully encompassing the Sao and Ya, broadly drawing on masters and collections — bamboo slips sweat and clouds finish; titled Rhyme Compendium, thirty fascicles in all, cut into a school of its own.

sentences.zh: 方可藏彼名山，副諸石室，見群玉之為淺，鄙懸金之不定。

translations.literal: Only then could it be stored on that famous mountain and deposited in the stone chamber — seeing the shallowness of the Jade Collection, disdaining the uncertainty of suspended gold.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could it be stored on that famous mountain and deposited in the stone chamber — seeing the shallowness of the Jade Collection, disdaining the uncertainty of suspended gold.

sentences.zh: 爰命末學，制其都序。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered this least scholar to compose its general preface.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered this least scholar to compose its general preface.

sentences.zh: 徽業術已寡，思理彌殫，心若死灰，文慚生氣。

translations.literal: Hui's learning and skill are already meager; my thinking is utterly exhausted — my heart like dead ash, my writing ashamed before living breath.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's learning and skill are already meager; my thinking is utterly exhausted — my heart like dead ash, my writing ashamed before living breath.

sentences.zh: 徒以犬馬識養，飛走懷仁，敢執顛沛之辭，遂操狂簡之筆。

translations.literal: Only because dogs and horses know how they are kept, and flying and running creatures cherish benevolence, do I dare take up words of hardship and wield this reckless, rough brush.
translations.idiomatic: Only because dogs and horses know how they are kept, and flying and running creatures cherish benevolence, do I dare take up words of hardship and wield this reckless, rough brush.

sentences.zh: 而齊魯富經學，楚鄭多良士，西河之彥，幸不誚于索居，東裡之才，請能加於潤色。

translations.literal: Yet Qi and Lu abound in classical learning; Chu and Zheng have many worthy scholars — may the eminent men of Xihe not scoff at solitary composition; may the talents of Dongli please add polish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi and Lu abound in classical learning; Chu and Zheng have many worthy scholars — may the eminent men of Xihe not scoff at solitary composition; may the talents of Dongli please add polish.

sentences.zh: 未幾，俊薨，晉王廣複引為揚州博士，令與諸儒撰《江都集禮》一部。

translations.literal: Before long Jun died; Prince of Jin Yang Guang again brought him in as Yangzhou Doctor and ordered him with various Confucians to compile one work, the Jiangdu Collected Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jun died; Prince of Jin Yang Guang again brought him in as Yangzhou Doctor and ordered him with various Confucians to compile one work, the Jiangdu Collected Rites.

sentences.zh: 複令徽作序曰：

translations.literal: He again ordered Hui to compose a preface, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He again ordered Hui to compose a preface, saying:

sentences.zh: 禮之為用至矣。

translations.literal: The use of ritual reaches its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The function of ritual is supreme.

sentences.zh: 大與天地同節，明與日月齊照，源開三本，體合四端。

translations.literal: Great — it shares its measure with Heaven and Earth; bright — it shines level with sun and moon; its source opens from the three roots; its substance joins the four beginnings.
translations.idiomatic: In grandeur it keeps pace with Heaven and Earth; in brilliance it shines with sun and moon; its origins reach back to the three foundations, its substance embraces the four cardinal virtues.

sentences.zh: 巢居穴處之前，即萌其理，龜文鳥跡以後，稍顯其事。

translations.literal: Before men dwelled in nests and caves, its principle already sprouted; after tortoise markings and bird tracks, its affairs gradually appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Even before men lived in nests and caves, its principles had already begun to form; after tortoise script and bird tracks appeared, its practices gradually came to light.

sentences.zh: 雖情存簡易，意非玉帛，而夏造殷因，可得知也。

translations.literal: Although the sentiment preserved simplicity and ease, and the intent was not jade and silk, yet Xia created and Yin followed — this can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Though the spirit favored simplicity and the meaning lay deeper than jade and silk offerings, how Xia fashioned ritual and Yin inherited it can still be discerned.

sentences.zh: 至如秩宗三禮之職，司徒五禮之官，邦國以和，人神惟敬，道德仁義，非此莫成，進退俯仰，去茲安適！

translations.literal: As for the Director of the Ancestral Temple with his three rites, the Minister of Education with his five rites — states and kingdoms are harmonized thereby, men and spirits revere thereby; virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness cannot be achieved without this; in advancing, retreating, bowing, and looking up — apart from this, where would one go!
translations.idiomatic: Consider the Director of the Ancestral Temple charged with the three rites, and the Minister of Education with the five — through them states find harmony and men and spirits find reverence; virtue, the Way, benevolence, and righteousness cannot be achieved without ritual; in every bow, every step, every glance, where else could one turn?

sentences.zh: 若璽印塗，猶防止水，豈直譬彼耕耨，均斯粉澤而已哉！

translations.literal: Like a seal's ink paste, it is as if blocking and stopping water — how could it merely be compared to plowing and hoeing, or to applying rouge and powder!
translations.idiomatic: Like the paste on a seal, it holds back chaos as a dike holds water — how could it be reduced to a mere analogy for tilling fields or applying cosmetics!

sentences.zh: 自世屬坑焚，時移漢、魏，叔孫通之碩解，高堂隆之博識，專門者霧集，製作者風馳，節文頗備，枝條互起。

translations.literal: From the age of the pit and burning, as times shifted through Han and Wei — Shusun Tong's great understanding, Gaotang Long's broad knowledge; specialists gathered like fog, compilers raced like wind; regulations and forms were largely complete, branches and twigs rose one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of the pit and the burning of books, through Han and Wei, masters like Shusun Tong and Gaotang Long brought their great learning; specialists gathered in droves and compilers worked at fever pitch until regulations were largely complete and branches of ritual proliferated.

sentences.zh: 皇帝負扆垂旒，辨方正位，纂勳華之曆象，綴文武之憲章。

translations.literal: The Emperor, leaning on the screen with pendants hanging, distinguished the directions and set positions right, compiled the calendar and omens of Yao and Shun, and joined together the statutes of King Wen and King Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, enthroned with screen and pendant tassels, set the directions aright and aligned all positions, gathering the calendrical wisdom of Yao and Shun and weaving together the institutions of King Wen and King Wu.

sentences.zh: 車書之所會通，觸境斯應，雲雨之所沾潤，無思不韙。

translations.literal: Where chariots and writing meet and connect, touching a border brings response; where clouds and rain moisten and enrich, no thought fails to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: Where chariots and writing converge, every frontier touched brings response; where cloud and rain spread their blessing, no aspiration goes unfulfilled.

sentences.zh: 東探石簣之符，西蠹羽陵之策，鳴鑾太室，偃伯靈台，樂備五常，禮兼八代。

translations.literal: Eastward he sought the talisman of the Stone Basket; westward he perused the plans of Yuling; he sounded his carriage bells at the Grand Chamber and rested the war-chariots at the Spirit Terrace; music was complete in the five constants, ritual embraced eight dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Eastward he sought the talisman of the Stone Basket; westward he studied the texts of Yuling; he sounded his bells at the Grand Chamber and stilled his war-chariots at the Spirit Terrace; music fulfilled the five constants, ritual spanned eight dynasties.

sentences.zh: 上柱國、太尉、揚州總管、晉王握珪璋之寶，履神明之德，隆化贊傑，藏用顯仁。

translations.literal: The Duke of Upper Pillar, Grand Commandant, General Director of Yangzhou, Prince of Jin — grasping the treasure of jade tablet and scepter, treading the virtue of the divine and bright, promoting transformation and assisting excellence, storing usefulness and displaying benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin, Duke of Upper Pillar, Grand Commandant, and General Director of Yangzhou — holding the jade tablet and scepter, embodying divine virtue, fostering transformation and nurturing talent, concealing his power yet revealing his benevolence.

sentences.zh: 地居周邵，業冠河楚，允文允武，多才多藝。

translations.literal: In territory he stood where Zhou and Shao had stood; in achievement he topped the He and Chu regions; truly literary and truly martial, of many talents and many arts.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stood where the Zhou dukes once ruled; his achievements surpassed those of the He and Chu lands; he was truly both literary and martial, gifted in many arts.

sentences.zh: 戎衣而籠關塞，朝服而掃江湖，收杞梓之才，辟康莊之館。

translations.literal: In martial garb he enclosed the passes and barriers; in court robes he swept the rivers and lakes; he gathered talents like qi and zi timber, and opened halls on the broad highway.
translations.idiomatic: In armor he secured the frontier passes; in court dress he pacified the rivers and lakes; he gathered men of talent as one gathers fine timber, and opened halls to welcome them on the king's highway.

sentences.zh: 加以佃漁六學，網羅百氏，繼稷下之絕軌，弘泗上之淪風，賾無隱而不探，事有難而必綜。

translations.literal: Moreover he tilled and fished the six schools, netted the hundred masters, continued the broken tracks of Jixia, and spread the submerged wind of Sishang; nothing hidden in the deep went unprobed, nothing difficult went unexamined.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he worked the six schools and gathered the hundred masters, reviving the lost traditions of Jixia and restoring the faded culture of Sishang; no hidden truth went unexplored, no difficult question unexamined.

sentences.zh: 至於采標綠錯，華垂丹篆，刑名長短，儒墨是非，書圃翰林之域，理窟談叢之內，謁者所求之餘，侍醫所校之逸，莫不澄涇辨渭，拾珠棄蚌。

translations.literal: As for colored headings and green interlines, splendor hanging in cinnabar seal script; the rights and wrongs of law and name, Confucian and Mohist; within the garden of books and forest of brush; within the caverns of principle and thickets of discourse; the surplus sought by petitioners, the stray texts collated by attending physicians — none went without clarifying Jing from Wei, picking pearls and discarding shells.
translations.idiomatic: Whether colored headings or cinnabar annotations, legal disputes or Confucian-Mohist debates, texts from the libraries of scholars or the recesses of debate — even stray volumes sought by petitioners or collated by court physicians — all were sifted to separate the clear from the muddy, keeping pearls and casting aside shells.

sentences.zh: 以為質文遞改，損益不同，《明堂》、《曲台》之記，南宮、東觀之說，鄭、王、徐、賀之答，崔、譙、何、瘐之論，簡牒雖盈，菁華蓋鮮。

translations.literal: He held that substance and ornament alternately changed, and increase and decrease differed — records like the Bright Hall and Qu Terrace, discussions of the Southern Palace and Eastern Watchtower, replies of Zheng, Wang, Xu, and He, treatises of Cui, Qiao, He, and Yu; though documents overflowed, the essential cream was scarce.
translations.idiomatic: He saw that substance and ornament had shifted through the ages, and that additions and subtractions varied — records such as the Bright Hall and Qu Terrace, discussions from the Southern Palace and Eastern Watchtower, the replies of Zheng, Wang, Xu, and He, the treatises of Cui, Qiao, He, and Yu; though documents abounded, fine essence was rare.

sentences.zh: 乃以宣條暇日，聽訟餘晨，娛情窺寶之鄉，凝相觀濤之岸，總括油素，躬披緗縹，芟蕪刈楚，振領提綱，去其繁雜，撮其指要，勒成一家，名曰《江都集禮》。

translations.literal: Thereupon, on days of leisure from proclaiming regulations, in the mornings left after hearing lawsuits, delighting the heart in the land of peering at treasures, gazing fixedly from the shore at watching the waves — he gathered oil-silk scrolls, personally unrolled red and blue bindings, cut weeds and reaped thorns, shook out collars and raised the net-rope, removed the complex and mixed, extracted the essential points, and cut them into one school, naming it the Jiangdu Collected Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Then, in leisure from governing and in mornings left after hearing cases, he turned to the treasury of learning and the shore of great design — gathering scrolls, unrolling bindings himself, clearing away weeds, setting the main theme and raising the guiding principle, stripping away complexity and extracting essentials until one unified work emerged, titled the Jiangdu Collected Rites.

sentences.zh: 凡十二帙，一百二十卷，取方月數，用比星周，軍國之義存焉，人倫之紀備矣。

translations.literal: In all twelve fascicles, one hundred twenty scrolls — taking the square of the number of months, used to compare with the cycle of stars; the meaning of army and state is preserved therein, the norms of human relations are complete.
translations.idiomatic: In all, twelve fascicles and one hundred twenty scrolls — the number squared like the months, compared to the cycle of stars — preserving the principles of state and army and completing the norms of human relations.

sentences.zh: 昔者龜、蒙令後，睢、渙名籓，誠複出警入蹕，擬乘輿之制度，建韣載旂，用天子之禮樂。

translations.literal: Formerly Gui and Meng were ordered to succeed, Sui and Huan were famed as feudatories — truly they again went out with guards and entered with cleared roads, imitating the institutions of the imperial carriage, establishing quivers and bearing banners, using the rites and music of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the lords of Gui and Meng were ordered to succeed their fathers, and Sui and Huan were famed feudatories — they indeed went abroad with imperial escort and returned with roads cleared, adopting the trappings of the imperial carriage, setting up quivers and bearing banners, and employing the Son of Heaven's rites and music.

sentences.zh: 求諸述作，未聞茲典。

translations.literal: Searching among writings and compositions, one has not heard of this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Search through all literary works — nowhere is such a canon to be found.

sentences.zh: 方可韜之Ｐ水，副彼名山，見刻石之非工，嗤懸金之已陋。

translations.literal: Only then could it be wrapped and hidden in the depths and deposited on that famous mountain, seeing that carving in stone was inadequate craft, and scoffing at the crudeness of suspended gold.
translations.idiomatic: Only then could it be wrapped away in secret depths and deposited on that famous mountain — seeing that stone carving was inadequate craft, and scoffing at the crudeness of hanging gold.

sentences.zh: 是知《沛王通論》，不獨擅于前修，《甯朔新書》，更追慚於往冊。

translations.literal: From this one knows that the Comprehensive Treatise of the Prince of Pei did not alone monopolize merit among earlier masters, and the New Book of Ningshuo would further be shamed when compared with past registers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we see that the Comprehensive Treatise of the Prince of Pei was not the sole masterpiece of earlier scholars, and the New Book of Ningshuo would blush in comparison with works of old.

sentences.zh: 徽幸樓仁岳，忝遊聖海，謬承恩獎，敢敘該博之致雲。

translations.literal: Hui, fortunate to ascend the tower of benevolence and virtue, unworthily roaming the sea of sagehood, wrongly receiving gracious reward, dares narrate the reaching of such comprehensiveness.
translations.idiomatic: I, Hui, fortunate to stand on the tower of benevolence, unworthy to swim in the sea of sagehood, have wrongly received such gracious favor — and dare here set forth the breadth of this achievement.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，詔徽與著作佐郎陸從典、太常博士褚亮、歐陽詢等助越公楊素撰《魏書》，會素薨而止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he ordered Hui, together with Editing Assistant Lu Congdian, Grand Master of Sacrifices Chu Liang, Ouyang Xun, and others, to assist Duke of Yue Yang Su in compiling the Book of Wei; it stopped when Su died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he ordered Hui, together with Editing Assistant Lu Congdian, Grand Master of Sacrifices Chu Liang, Ouyang Xun, and others, to assist Duke of Yue Yang Su in compiling the Book of Wei; the project halted when Su died.

sentences.zh: 授京兆郡博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Doctor of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Doctor of Jingzhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感兄弟甚重之，數相來往。

translations.literal: The brothers Yang Xuangan greatly valued him, and they frequently visited one another.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Yang Xuangan held him in high esteem, and they visited one another frequently.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，凡交關多罹其患。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, all who had associations with him mostly suffered calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuangan was defeated, nearly everyone who had dealings with him fell into trouble.

sentences.zh: 徽以玄感故人，為帝所不悅，有司希旨，出徽為西海郡威定縣主簿。

translations.literal: Because Hui was an old friend of Xuangan, the Emperor was displeased with him; the officials, seeking to please, transferred Hui out to be Chief Clerk of Weiding county, Xihai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hui was an old friend of Xuangan, the Emperor took displeasure with him; the officials, reading his mood, transferred Hui to the post of Chief Clerk of Weiding County in Xihai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 意甚不平，行至隴西，發病卒。

translations.literal: His mind was greatly resentful; traveling as far as Longxi, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply embittered, he set out for his new post; en route through Longxi he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 杜正玄 弟:正藏杜正玄，字慎徽，其先本京兆人，八世祖曼，為石趙從事中郎，因家於鄴。

translations.literal: Du Zhengxuan — younger brother: Zhengcang. Du Zhengxuan, styled Shenhui, his ancestors were originally natives of Jingzhao; his eighth-generation ancestor Man served as Attendant Gentleman of the Stone Zhao, and the family settled in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhengxuan — Du Zhengxuan, styled Shenhui, whose ancestors were originally from Jingzhao; his eighth-generation ancestor Man served as Attendant Gentleman under the Stone Zhao, and the family then settled in Ye.

sentences.zh: 自曼至正玄，世以文學相授。

translations.literal: From Man down to Zhengxuan, the family transmitted literary learning from generation to generation.
translations.idiomatic: From Man down to Zhengxuan, literary learning was handed down through the family for generations.

sentences.zh: 正玄尤聰敏，博涉多通。

translations.literal: Zhengxuan was especially clever and quick, broadly versed and masterful in many fields.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengxuan was especially quick-witted, widely learned, and masterful in many fields.

sentences.zh: 兄弟數人，俱未弱冠，並以文章才辨籍甚三河之間。

translations.literal: Several brothers, all not yet twenty, were all famed between the Three Rivers for literary composition and eloquent debate.
translations.idiomatic: Several brothers, none yet twenty, were all renowned throughout the Three Rivers region for their writing and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，舉秀才，尚書試方略，正玄應對如響，下筆成章。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang he was recommended as xiucai; the Ministry tested strategy and methods — Zhengxuan answered like an echo, and putting brush to paper completed compositions.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era he was recommended as xiucai; when the Ministry tested him on strategy and policy, Zhengxuan answered without hesitation and wrote finished compositions at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 僕射楊素負才傲物，正玄抗辭酬對，無所屈撓，素甚不悅。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang Su, relying on talent and arrogant toward others, met Zhengxuan's bold replies in debate — nowhere yielding — and Su was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Su, proud of his talent and arrogant toward others, found Zhengxuan answering his challenges without yielding; Su was greatly displeased.

sentences.zh: 久之，會林邑獻白鸚鵡，素促召正玄，使者相望。

translations.literal: After some time, when Linyi presented a white parrot, Su urgently summoned Zhengxuan; messengers followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, when Linyi presented a white parrot, Su urgently summoned Zhengxuan, dispatching messenger after messenger.

sentences.zh: 及至，即令作賦。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Su immediately ordered him to compose a fu.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Su immediately ordered him to compose a rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 正玄倉卒之際，援筆立成。

translations.literal: At this hurried moment, Zhengxuan took up the brush and completed it at once.
translations.idiomatic: Under this sudden demand, Zhengxuan took up his brush and finished at once.

sentences.zh: 素見文不加點，始異之。

translations.literal: Su saw the text needed no corrections, and began to regard him as unusual.
translations.idiomatic: Su saw that the text needed not a single correction, and began to regard him with new respect.

sentences.zh: 因令更擬諸雜文筆十餘條，又皆立成，而辭理華贍，素乃歎曰：「此真秀才，吾不及也！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered him further to draft more than ten items of various miscellaneous writings; again all were completed at once, and the wording and reasoning were splendid. Su then sighed and said: 'This is a true xiucai — I cannot match him!
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered him to draft more than ten miscellaneous compositions; again all were finished at once, and the language and reasoning were splendid. Su sighed and said, "This is a true xiucai — I cannot match him!

sentences.zh: 授晉王行參軍，轉豫章王記室，卒官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Adjutant to the Prince of Jin, transferred to Recorder for the Prince of Yuzhang, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Adjutant to the Prince of Jin, then transferred to Recorder for the Prince of Yuzhang, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弟正藏。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Zhengcang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Zhengcang.

sentences.zh: 正藏字為善，尤好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zhengcang, styled Weishan, especially loved learning and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengcang, styled Weishan, was devoted to learning and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，授純州行參軍，曆下邑正。

translations.literal: At twenty he was recommended as xiucai, appointed Adjutant of Chunzhou, and served successively as magistrate of lower counties.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recommended as xiucai, appointed Adjutant of Chunzhou, and served in succession as magistrate of lesser counties.

sentences.zh: 大業中，學業該通，應詔舉秀才，兄弟三人俱以文章一時詣闕，論者榮之。

translations.literal: During Daye, his learning was comprehensive and penetrating; responding to an edict he was recommended as xiucai; three brothers together, by their literary compositions, at one time went to the court — commentators honored them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era, his learning was comprehensive; summoned by imperial edict as xiucai, all three brothers traveled to court together on the strength of their writing — a feat commentators praised.

sentences.zh: 著碑誄銘頌詩賦百餘篇。

translations.literal: He composed more than one hundred pieces of stele inscriptions, dirges, eulogies, hymns, poems, and fu.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote more than one hundred stele inscriptions, dirges, eulogies, hymns, poems, and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 又著《文章體式》，大為後進所寶，時人號為文軌，乃至海外高麗、百濟，亦共傳習，稱為《杜家新書》。

translations.literal: He also composed Literary Forms and Styles, greatly treasured by later students; people of the time called it the Track of Letters, and even overseas in Goguryeo and Baekje they jointly transmitted and studied it, calling it the New Book of the Du Family.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Literary Forms and Styles, which later scholars greatly treasured; contemporaries called it the Track of Letters, and even in distant Goguryeo and Baekje it was transmitted and studied under the name New Book of the Du Family.

sentences.zh: 常得志京兆常得志，博學善屬文，官至秦王記室。

translations.literal: Chang Dezhi — Chang Dezhi of Jingzhao, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, rose to the office of Recorder to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Dezhi — Chang Dezhi of Jingzhao, a man of broad learning skilled at literary composition, rose to the post of Recorder to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 及王薨，過故宮，為五言詩，辭理悲壯，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: When the prince died, passing the former palace he composed a five-character poem; its wording and reasoning were mournful and heroic, and it was greatly valued by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince died, Chang passed the former palace and composed a five-character poem — mournful and heroic in tone — that contemporaries greatly admired.

sentences.zh: 複為《兄弟論》，義理可稱。

translations.literal: He also composed A Treatise on Brothers; its principles and reasoning were commendable.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote A Treatise on Brothers, whose reasoning was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 尹式河間尹式，博學解屬文，少有令問。

translations.literal: Yin Shi — Yin Shi of Hejian, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, from youth had a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shi — Yin Shi of Hejian, broadly learned and skilled at literary composition, enjoyed a fine reputation from youth.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，官至漢王記室，王甚重之，及漢王敗，式自殺。

translations.literal: During Renshou he rose to Recorder to the Prince of Han; the prince greatly valued him, and when the Prince of Han was defeated, Shi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he served as Recorder to the Prince of Han, who held him in high esteem; when the prince was defeated, Yin Shi took his own life.

sentences.zh: 其族人正卿、彥卿俱有俊才，名顯於世劉善經河間劉善經，博物洽聞，尤善詞筆。

translations.literal: His clansmen Zhengqing and Yanqing both had outstanding talent and were famed in the world. Liu Shanjing — Liu Shanjing of Hejian, broadly learned and well informed, especially skilled at literary phrasing and brushwork.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen Zhengqing and Yanqing both had outstanding talent and were famed in the world. Liu Shanjing — Liu Shanjing of Hejian, a man of wide learning and broad knowledge, especially skilled with words and the pen.

sentences.zh: 曆仕著作佐郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He successively served as Editing Assistant and Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Editing Assistant and Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 著《酬德傳》三十卷，《諸劉譜》三十卷，《四聲指歸》一卷，行於世。
