translations.literal: He composed Returning Favor Biographies in thirty scrolls, Genealogies of the Various Lius in thirty scrolls, and Guide to the Four Tones in one scroll — all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Returning Favor Biographies in thirty scrolls, Genealogies of the Various Lius in thirty scrolls, and Guide to the Four Tones in one scroll — all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 祖君彥范陽祖君彥，齊尚書僕射孝徵之子也。

translations.literal: Zu Junyan — Zu Junyan of Fanyang, son of Xiao Zheng, Vice Director of the Ministry of Works of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Junyan — Zu Junyan of Fanyang, son of Zu Xiao Zheng, Vice Director of the Ministry of Works under Qi.

sentences.zh: 容貌短小，言辭訥澀，有才學。

translations.literal: His appearance was short and small, his speech halting and awkward, yet he had talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Short in stature and halting in speech, he nevertheless possessed talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 大業末，官至東平郡書佐。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he rose to Secretary Aide of Dongping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he served as Secretary Aide of Dongping Commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡陷於翟讓，因為李密所得。

translations.literal: The commandery fell to Zhai Rang, and he was thereby obtained by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When the commandery fell to Zhai Rang, Zu came into the hands of Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密甚禮之，署為記室，軍書羽檄，皆成於其手。

translations.literal: Mi greatly honored him, appointing him Recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches all were completed by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi treated him with great respect and appointed him Recorder; military documents and urgent dispatches all issued from his hand.

sentences.zh: 及密敗，為王世充所殺。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, he was killed by Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi was defeated, Zu was killed by Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 孔德紹會稽孔德紹，有清才，官至景城縣丞。

translations.literal: Kong Deshao — Kong Deshao of Kuaiji, possessed refined talent, and rose to Assistant Magistrate of Jingcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Deshao — Kong Deshao of Kuaiji, a man of refined talent, rose to the post of Assistant Magistrate of Jingcheng County.

sentences.zh: 竇建德稱王，署為中書令，專典書檄。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande declared himself king, he appointed him Director of the Secretariat, exclusively in charge of documents and dispatches.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande declared himself king, he appointed Kong Director of the Secretariat, putting him exclusively in charge of official documents and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande was defeated, Kong was executed.

sentences.zh: 劉斌南陽劉斌，頗有詞藻，官至信都郡司功書佐。

translations.literal: Liu Bin — Liu Bin of Nanyang, possessed considerable literary ornament, and rose to Secretary Aide in the Merit Office of Xindu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin — Liu Bin of Nanyang, a man of considerable literary polish, rose to Secretary Aide in the Merit Office of Xindu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 竇建德署為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande appointed him Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande appointed him Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，複為劉闥中書侍郎，與劉闥亡歸突厥，不知所終。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, he again served Liu Heita as Vice Director of the Secretariat; together with Liu Heita he fled and returned to the Turks — his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande was defeated, Liu served Liu Heita as Vice Director of the Secretariat; he fled with Liu Heita to the Turks, and his ultimate fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏文有言「古今文人，類不護細行，鮮能以名節自立」，信矣！

translations.literal: The historian says: Cao Pi had a saying — 'Men of letters ancient and modern generally do not guard small conduct; few can establish themselves by name and integrity' — how true!
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Cao Pi once said, "Literary men of every age generally neglect small proprieties; few can stand on their reputation and integrity alone" — how true that is!

sentences.zh: 王胄、虞綽之輩，崔儦、孝逸之倫，或矜氣負才，遺落世事，或學優命薄，調高位下，心鬱抑而孤憤，志盤桓而不定，嘯傲當世，脫略公卿。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, Yu Chuo, and their sort; Cui Biao, Xiaoyi, and their kind — some proud in spirit and relying on talent, casting off worldly affairs; some excellent in learning but thin in fate, appointed high yet stationed low; hearts depressed and solitary in resentment, wills wandering and unsettled; whistling proudly in the age, casting off restraint toward lords and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou, Yu Chuo, and their like; Cui Biao, Wang Zhen, and their kind — some proud of their talent and disdainful of worldly affairs; some scholars of great learning but ill fortune, nominally promoted yet kept low; hearts sunk in resentment, wills unsettled and adrift; defiant toward their age and careless of high officials.

sentences.zh: 是知跅弛見遺，嫉邪忤物，不獨漢陽趙壹、平原禰衡而已。

translations.literal: From this one knows that being unrestrained and cast aside, hating evil and offending others — this was not limited to Zhao Yi of Hanyang and Mi Heng of Pingyuan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thus we see that being unrestrained and cast aside, hating injustice and offending others — this was not the fate of Zhao Yi of Hanyang and Mi Heng of Pingyuan alone.

sentences.zh: 故多離咎悔，鮮克有終。

translations.literal: Therefore many met blame and regret, and few achieved good endings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore many met blame and regret, and few came to good ends.

sentences.zh: 然其學涉稽古，文詞辨麗，並鄧林之一枝，昆山之片玉矣。

translations.literal: Yet their learning reached into antiquity, and their literary phrasing was clear and beautiful — each a branch of the Deng Forest, a shard of jade from Kun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their learning reached deep into antiquity, and their writing was clear and beautiful — each a branch of the sacred forest, a shard of jade from Kun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 有隋總一寰宇，得人為盛，秀異之貢，不過十數。

translations.literal: When Sui unified all within the four seas, gaining men was its glory; outstanding and exceptional submissions numbered no more than a dozen or so.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui unified the realm, its greatest strength lay in the men it gathered — yet outstanding talents numbered scarcely a dozen.

sentences.zh: 正玄昆季三人預焉，華萼相耀，亦為難兄弟矣。

translations.literal: Three brothers of Zhengxuan were among them; flower and calyx shining upon each other — they too were rare brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers of the Zhengxuan family were among them — flowers and calyxes shining together — a brotherhood truly hard to match.
